And I said: By no means, Lord, Lord; they say to me: Is not this which is spoken a parable?") What Set (or make firm) your face means, we have said more fully above; for there is need of firmness of countenance and hardness of brow, so that the prophet may speak fearlessly the things he is commanded, above all when sad things must be announced to the whole multitude of the people. Now what 'Theman' and 'Darom' and 'Nageb', and again 'Nageb', for which the Seventy translated ἀπηλιὼτην [Apeliotes, the east wind], signify in the Hebrew, our translation has expressed. And as for their saying 'leader Nageb', the Hebrew has it better, 'of the field' or 'of the southern region'; for what is written is not 'sare', as the Seventy supposed, a word that means 'leader' and 'prince', but 'sade', which properly signifies 'field' and 'region'; and the error grew up because of the likeness of the letters 'daleth' [d] and 'res' [r]. The divine word, then, speaks through the μεταφορὰν [metaphor] of a forest against Jerusalem, which is a dwelling of beasts and of fierce men, saying that he will set it on fire and that all its wood will be burned up together; by no means does he call trees those that were lacking in fruit, but wood, as if made ready for burning. And first he burns in it the green wood, according to what we read in this same prophet: And begin from my holy ones, and afterward the dry, which could have nothing living in itself; that is, the saints and the sinners together, so that some by captivity may escape an evil death, while others are handed over to eternal punishments. And what he adds, From the south to the north, indicates this: from Jerusalem to Babylon, so that the whole road of those going into captivity may be filled with those falling by sword, famine and pestilence; for to those who are in Babylon, Jerusalem lies to the south, just as, conversely, the pot of Jeremiah, which signifies Jerusalem, is kindled from the face of the north, that is, of Babylon. And beautifully, at the beginning: Drip, he says, toward the southwest, so that not the whole wrath of God may seem to be poured out, but a kind of drip and a part. But if there is such savagery in a drip, what must be reckoned of whole downpours, so that all flesh, which is to see the salvation of God, may know through the burning of the woods and through the flame that is extinguished by no one's help that he himself is the Lord? Understanding this, the prophet answered: Ah, ah, ah, Lord God (or, as the Seventy translated: By no means, Lord), and he adds: They say to me: Does not this man speak in parables? (or: Is this a parable which is spoken?), and the sense is: 'Speak more plainly; we do not understand what you are saying in a parable; open to us the meaning of God in plain speech'. Tropologically, however, Theman and Nageb and Darom can be understood as Egypt; for we read in Daniel that the south is frequently taken for Egypt; and Egypt refers to the straits of this world. Ezekiel therefore prophesies the evils that are to come upon the world, which he calls a forest, one that has no fruit-bearing trees but is a dwelling-place of beasts, of which it is also said in Psalm 28 (29): The voice of the Lord perfecting the stags, and he will uncover the thickets of the woods. These are the woods and forests that devoured more of Absalom's army in the battle than the sword killed. And in the forests the green wood is kindled first, and then the dry: those who live in evil, and those who are dead to righteousness. And what is said, And every face shall be burned in it from the south to the north, says this: from those who seemed to be fervent in spirit to those who, as iniquity increased and the love of many grew cold, have lost their former warmth, so that all flesh may perceive that the flame of the Lord is not extinguished. And the prophet prays that what the Lord has threatened may not come to pass, that is, that the forest may not be set on fire and all the wood burned up together, so that either they may still receive room for repentance, or the necessity of announcing sad things may not be laid upon him, especially since the people do not understand them and are provoked rather to madness by the obscurity of the sayings.

21:1-5

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and distil toward the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the ground of Israel. And you shall say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will cast out my sword from its sheath, and I will kill in you the righteous and the wicked. But because I have killed in you the righteous and the wicked, my sword shall go forth from its sheath against all flesh, from the south to the north, and all flesh shall know that I the Lord have drawn my sword from its sheath, irrevocable. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and set firm your face against Jerusalem, and look toward their holy places, and prophesy over the land of Israel. And you shall say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw out my sword from its sheath, and I will slay out of you the lawless and the unrighteous. Because I will destroy out of you the lawless and the unrighteous, so shall my sword go forth from its sheath upon all flesh, from the south as far as the north, and all flesh shall know that I the Lord have drawn my sword from its sheath; it shall not return any more.") Because he had said above: They say of me: Does not this man speak in parables?, and the people were demanding a plain statement, therefore the Lord now says more plainly what he had spoken through a metaphor, or 'parable', and, as others rendered it, 'proverb': that the forests of Nageb and Darom and Theman [Hebrew words for the south] are Jerusalem and its temple and the Holy of Holies and the whole land of Judea, and that the flame which was to burn up the forest is to be understood as the devouring sword, which has been drawn from its sheath to kill the righteous and the wicked — for this is the green wood and the dry; whence the Lord also says: If they do such things, he says, in the green wood, what will they do in the dry? —; in place of which the Seventy, intending I know not what, translated 'the lawless and the unrighteous', as though both did not signify the same thing. And what he had said there: And all flesh shall see that I the Lord have kindled it, that is, the forest or the flame, and it shall not be quenched, here he says in other words: That all flesh may know that I the Lord have drawn my sword from its sheath, irrevocable. For truly, for Jerusalem the flame has not been lulled to sleep, nor the fire quenched, nor the sword recalled, because there was a short time in between, and Jerusalem, with its temple, was set ablaze by Babylonian fire.

21:6-7

And you, son of man, groan in the breaking of the loins, and in bitternesses groan before them. And when they say to you: Why do you groan?, you shall say: For the report, because it comes, and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be loosened, and every spirit shall grow weak, and waters shall flow down all knees; behold, it comes, and it shall be done, says the Lord. (LXX: "And you, son of man, groan in the breaking of your loins, and in griefs groan in their sight. And it shall be, if they say to you: Why do you groan?, then you shall say: Because of the tidings, because it comes, and every heart shall be seized, and all hands shall be loosened, and all flesh and every spirit shall be tested, and all thighs shall be defiled with moisture; behold, it comes, and it shall be, says the Lord God.") First he had said: 'Prophesy, or distil, toward the south, the southwest and the noonday, and toward the southern forest'. Because this seemed obscure, and the people did not understand the prophet's words, in the second place it is set down more plainly that the southern forest is Jerusalem, and that all the unfruitful trees, at whose roots the axe has been laid, are to be understood as its inhabitants, and that the sword is to be interpreted in place of the fire. In the third place the prophet is commanded that, since they are silent and do not ask why he has prophesied these things, he should do something by which he may be questioned, and should answer what the Lord has spoken. 'Groan', he says, 'and wail, not with a light voice nor with moderate grief, but in the breaking of the loins, so that your groaning may be brought forth from your inmost bowels and from bitterness of soul; and you shall do this before them so that, when they have asked you why you are crushed with such great groaning and what evil has befallen you that you groan so, you may answer them with my word: This is why I lament and cannot hide the grief of my heart, because the report which had always sounded in my ears is being fulfilled in deed, and it comes — the menace, that is, of the raging Babylonian army; and when it has come and has hemmed Jerusalem in with a rampart, then every heart shall melt and all hands shall be loosened, so that, with panic seizing men's minds, no one dares to resist; for the spirit of all the warriors shall grow weak, and such trembling and dread shall seize them all that, under the compulsion of fear, their limbs and bowels are loosened and the bladder cannot hold its moisture, so that their knees are defiled with urine' — for it is natural that, under the compulsion of fear, the bladder is relaxed and, against a man's will, the moisture flows down; which indeed also tends to happen in the severity of illnesses, that, after the strength of the sick has failed, not only the knees but even the beds are defiled —. 'Behold', he says, 'it comes, what I have often foretold and what is being fulfilled in deed, and it shall be done, which not I but the Lord has spoken'. I know that a certain man unrolled many testimonies on the breaking of the loins and the flowing waters, so that the prophet's chastity might be made out, and the bitterness of soul and the inward pain of mind, namely that the waters of seed defile the knees; but this exposition does not belong to the present passage.

21:8-17

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy, and you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: Speak. The sword, the sword is sharpened and filed; it is sharpened to slaughter victims, and it is filed that it may gleam: you who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree. And I have given it to be polished, that it may be held in the hand; this sword is sharpened, and this one is filed, that it may be in the hand of the slayer. Cry out and howl, son of man, because this one has come among my people, this one among all the leaders of Israel who had fled; they have been handed over to the sword with my people, therefore clap upon your thigh, because it has been proved, and this when it has overturned the scepter and it shall be no more, says the Lord God. You therefore, son of man, prophesy, and strike hand against hand, and let the sword be doubled, and let the sword of the slain be tripled. This is the sword of great slaughter, which makes them stand aghast, and melt in heart, and multiplies the ruins. In all their gates I have set the confusion of the sword, sharpened and filed to flash, clad for slaughter. Be sharpened, go to the right or to the left, wherever the desire of your face is. Moreover I too will clap hand against hand, and I will fulfill my indignation; I the Lord have spoken. (It is too much if I set down both editions, and the length of the books is drawn out, especially where there is either no difference or a small one; I will therefore set down some of the things that disagree. Where we said: You who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree, they translated: Kill, despise, reject every tree; again, where we said: Who had fled, have been handed over to the sword, both they and others translated: My guests, or inhabitants; and where we said: Clap upon the thigh, they put: Strike the hand; and where we translated: And this when it has overturned the scepter, their edition has: The tribe has been rejected.) He speaks, moreover, to the sword of Nebuchadnezzar, that it should come against Jerusalem and be sharpened and filed, for many must be slaughtered; and he makes an apostrophe to it: 'You are the one who moves and overturns the scepter of my son, namely the rule of the people of Israel, and you cut down every tree, the whole multitude of the people. I have given', he says, 'this sword to be held in the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, and to be in the hand of a most powerful man. Therefore, O prophet, cry out and howl, and bear witness to the impending evils with the lamentation of your voice. This sword has spared no one, nor left anyone without a share in the impending evils. It has come among the people, it has come among the leaders of Israel, it has come among my guests and the priests who dwelt in my temple. Therefore strike your thigh, or your hand, and take on the bearing of a mourner. For this sword has been proved by me, and this when it has overturned my scepter and kingdom, which shall be no more and shall come to its end in King Zedekiah. Again I command you, prophet, that you, who had struck your thigh in astonishment and wonder, should strike your hands also, so that not only once but a second and a third time the sword may come to slay'. For Nebuchadnezzar had come the first time when he carried off Jeconiah, and the second time when Jehoiakim reigned, the third time when Zedekiah did. 'And this is the tripled sword, when a great slaughter took place, and it multiplied the ruins to such a degree that they were stunned in mind and melted in heart, and it caused confusion in all their gates'. It is commanded therefore to it, that is, to the sword sharpened and filed to flash, clad and ready and prepared for slaughter, that it go to the right if it so wishes, or to the left. 'Wherever', he says, 'it pleases your face, enter boldly, having me as your leader and helper. I will clap hand against hand, so that, as your patron and exhorter, I may spur you on as you rage against my adversaries. Do not hesitate, do not dread and fear to suffer what Sennacherib suffered; I the Lord have spoken; you are the minister of my will, carry out my sentence'. According to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense] we can take the sharpened sword, prepared for slaughter, as the devil, of whom the Apostle says: To hand over such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved; and in another place: Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme; and in the Psalms it is written: He sent fury and wrath and distress, a sending by most evil angels. Some think that this sword was also in the hand of the angel when Jerusalem was struck under David. Others, however, suspect that it is also said of that sword of which it is written in the Gospel: 'I came not to send peace upon the earth, but a sword, and to divide among themselves every bond of kinship, so that the wicked may fall and the saints rise again'. But it is impious to believe this of the Savior's sword, and not rather of the devil, who overturns the scepters of the Lord in the Church, who slays all among the people, both the leaders and the guests of God, and is then approved by the Lord, when he has overturned Judas the traitor and those like him; into whom, after he had eaten the morsel, Satan entered. And the sword of the slain is doubled and tripled, so that the sin of Jerusalem may be loosed, because she has received from the hand of the Lord her sins twofold. The Lord, moreover, rejoices and exults, and is the exhorter of the raging sword, that it may go either to the right or to the left, and wherever the desire of its face carries it, so that, the wicked being slain, the good may remain, and that which is written may be fulfilled: What has chaff to do with wheat?, says the Lord.

21:18-24

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, set for yourself two ways, and let the sword of the king of Babylon come: both shall go forth from one land; and with his hand he shall take a conjecture, at the head of the way of the city he shall cast it. You shall set a way for the sword to come to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah, into Jerusalem the most fortified. For the king of Babylon stood at the fork, at the head of the two ways, seeking divination, mixing arrows; he questioned idols, he consulted entrails. At his right hand the divination came out against Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth in slaughter, to lift up the voice in howling, to set battering rams against the gates, to heap up a mound, to build siege works. And in their eyes he shall be as one consulting an oracle in vain, and imitating the idleness of the sabbaths; but he himself will remember the iniquity, so as to capture. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have called your iniquities to remembrance, and have uncovered your transgressions, and your sins have appeared in all your thoughts; because, I say, you have called them to remembrance, you shall be taken by the hand. I know that in this place, following the Seventy translators, I have read a manifold exposition, which refers Rabbath of the Ammonites to the people of the nations, but Judah and Jerusalem to those who are gathered under the name of Christ and are given by their deeds the dignity of the name; and holds that the king of confusion, the devil, stands at every head of the ways and lies in ambush in secret, and that that little verse is fulfilled: Beside the path they have set a stumbling block for me; and that he stands at the fork, desiring either to hold those who are his own or to acquire new servitude for himself, and always goes to the right, namely to those who are placed on the right side, to storm them, to exult in slaughter, to capture wretched Jerusalem with battering rams and the heaping up of earthly works; and that at first indeed he seems to her to do nothing and to strive in vain, but, as he recalls the iniquities of those who dwell in the Church — or rather, by their evil works they bring the adverse powers back to the remembrance of their former crimes —, all the sins of the people and their thoughts are laid bare, and therefore they are captured, because they have heaped new offenses upon old ones. Another may have said these things; we must pursue the truth of the history we have begun. 'When', he says, 'the divine word had said to me: Prophesy, son of man, and speak to the sword, and say: The sword, the sword, and the rest that the prophecy of the sword contains, a second time the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Do you wish, son of man, to know who this sword is, and to learn more openly the person of the raging sword? Listen to what I say: Set two ways, so that by them the sword of the king of Babylon may come, who will indeed go forth by the one road of the Chaldeans but, when he has come through the desert and the wilderness to the fork of the land of Arabia which is called that of the Ammonites, of which one way leads to Jerusalem on the right-hand side, but the left to Rabbath of the Ammonites' — which is a metropolis and today is named Philadelphia. 'Mindful', he says, 'of the slaughter that befell the Assyrian king when a hundred and eighty-five thousand were cut down in one night, he will be afraid to turn aside to the right-hand side and go against most fortified Jerusalem, but he will stand at the very crossroads and, according to the rite of his nation, will consult the oracle, putting arrows into the quiver and mixing them, inscribed or marked with the names of each, to see whose arrow comes out and which city he ought to attack first' — this the Greeks call βελομαντίαν [belomancy, divination by arrows] or ῥαβδομαντίαν [rhabdomancy, divination by rods] —. 'He questioned the idols, therefore, he consulted the entrails. To the right came his divination, that he should go against Jerusalem and attack it, heap up mounds, set battering rams, build siege works and shut in the city, and in slaughter open his mouth and rouse the roar of an exulting and howling army. Doing this', he says, 'he will seem to the inhabitants of Jerusalem to consult the oracle in vain, and as it were to wear away the idleness of the sabbaths, namely to play and accomplish no work. But the king of Babylon will trust not in his own strength but in the iniquity of the people, by which he knows that they have offended God and have heaped up the sins of their fathers with new offenses, and that their transgressions have been laid open to all; and therefore he will not doubt of victory, because he will trust in the iniquity of Jerusalem'. This is according to the Hebrew, from which the Seventy disagree in most places, not so much in sense as in words.

21:25-27

But you, profane, wicked leader of Israel, whose day has come, foreordained in the time of iniquity, thus says the Lord God: Take off the miter, take away the crown; is not this that which raised up the lowly and brought low the lofty? Iniquity, iniquity, iniquity I will set it; and this shall not be until he comes whose is the judgment, and I will deliver it to him. (LXX: "And you, profane, lawless leader of Israel, whose day has come in the time of iniquity, the end, thus says the Lord God: You have taken off the miter and put on the crown; this shall not be alike; you have humbled the lofty and raised up the lowly. Iniquity, iniquity I will set it; nor shall this be such, until he comes to whom it is due, and I will give it to him.") Symmachus translated this passage thus: But you, profane, lawless leader of Israel, whose day has come, appointed in the time of iniquity, thus says the Lord God: He has taken off the miter and taken away the crown; neither this nor that; he has raised up the lowly and brought low the lofty. Iniquity, iniquity, iniquity I will make it; and this was not he whose is the judgment, whom I am going to give. After the overthrow of the city of Jerusalem and the captivity of the people, the word is directed to the leader of Israel, whom no one doubts to signify Zedekiah, in whom the rule of the kings of Israel from the stock of David came to an end. 'There has come to you', he says, 'the day which was foreordained against you long ago, and because of you the priesthood and the kingdom of the Jewish people perished'. For the miter is the insignia of the high priest; the crown, that is, the diadem, is the mark of a king. 'Is not this the miter and this the crown, which did nothing by judgment but, in imitation of the Babylonian king: Whom he wished he exalted, and whom he wished he humbled? Therefore, not once nor — according to the Seventy — twice, but a third time I will set iniquity upon you forever, which was not reckoned to you at once, but until Christ comes, whose is the judgment, and the Father delivers to him the kingdom and the priesthood, or the Church gathered from the nations'. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son; and in another place: O God, he says, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son; this is he for whom the everlasting rule and priesthood are laid up, of whom Jacob also spoke: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he shall be the expectation of the nations. In the place where we translated: Is not this, Symmachus rendered beautifully: Neither this nor that; for because he had said: Take off the miter, take away the crown, he added: 'Neither this nor that is', that is: 'Both the kingdom and the priesthood shall cease'. Hence, of those who afterwards, until the coming of Christ, were kings and priests alike, one, Hyrcanus the high priest, placed a diadem on his own head and wished in vain to claim both this and that for himself, since the kingdom was not owed to him after Zedekiah, but to him for whom it was laid up and who was the expectation of the nations; of whom Malachi also speaks: You priests, who defile my name, and a little after: My will is not in you, and I will not accept victims from your hands. For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place sacrifice is made and a pure offering is offered to my name; which pure offering, without the blood of goats, rams and bulls, is fulfilled at the coming of Christ, when he who is desired by the nations has come, and the sun of righteousness has risen, in whose wings is healing.

21:28-32

And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God, to the Ammonites and to their reproach; and you shall say: Blade, blade, unsheathe yourself to slay, file yourself that you may kill and flash, while vain things were seen for you and lies were divined, that you might be set upon the necks of the wounded wicked, whose day has come, foreordained in the time of iniquity; return to your sheath, to the place in which you were created; in the land of your birth I will judge you, and I will pour out my indignation upon you, in the fire of my fury I will blow upon you, and I will give you into the hands of foolish men and of those who fashion destruction. You shall be food for the fire, your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be given over to oblivion, because I the Lord have spoken. That the sword of the king of Babylon stood at the head of two ways, at the crossroads of the right and the left, of which one led to Jerusalem, the other to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and that the lot came out that he should go first against Jerusalem, we have read above; and, now that it has been stormed and taken, he foretells that its kingdom also and its priesthood have perished forever. What remained concerned the Ammonites, and the very order of the division called for it: what had become of the left-hand way. Hence the prophet is commanded to speak to the Ammonites and to their reproach, that they themselves are to be captured, and he directs his speech to the same sword: 'O blade, blade, you who are prepared for slaughter, who are filed so that you may flash and kill, although the idols have given you answers, and all that is answered by demons is vain, so that you might, namely, hang over the necks of the wounded and that through you might be fulfilled what the Lord had long threatened, nevertheless, once your work is completed which you did against the Ammonites, return to your sheath, that is, into Babylon, to the place in which you were made and created, so that in the land of your birth I may judge you and pour out my indignation upon you, and you may be captured by the might of the Medes and Persians'; which is said more fully in the volume of Isaiah, in the vision against Babylon: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them; and a little after: And that Babylon, glorious among kingdoms, renowned in the pride of the Chaldeans, shall be as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It shall not be inhabited to the end. And because he was once speaking under the person of the sword about the king, or rather the kingdom, of Babylon, he keeps the μεταφορὰν [metaphor]. 'In the fire', he says, 'of my fury I will blow upon you, so as to have you consumed by fire; and I will hand you over to the hands of foolish and unskilled men, who have not the art of forging and sharpening swords, so that you may by no means be sharpened any more, be filed and flash to kill, but may be food for the fire, and your blood, which you shed with all looking on, may rather flow back upon you; and you shall be handed over to eternal oblivion; and may you perish forever, because I the Lord have spoken these things, for whom to have said is to have done'.

22:1-16

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, will you not judge the city of bloods? And you shall show her all her abominations, and you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: A city shedding blood in her midst, so that her time may come; and which made idols against herself, so as to be polluted. By your blood, which has been shed by you, you have sinned; and in your idols which you made you are polluted; and you have made your days draw near, and you have brought on the time of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all lands. Those that are near and those that are far from you will triumph over you (or will mock you), filthy one, noble one, great in ruin. Behold, the princes of Israel, each in his own arm, have been in you to shed blood. Father and mother they have treated with insults in you (or they have cursed father and mother), the stranger they have falsely accused in your midst, the orphan and the widow they have grieved (or have oppressed) in you. My sanctuaries you have despised and my sabbaths you have polluted. Men who are detractors (or robbers) have been in you to shed blood, and upon the mountains they have eaten in you; wickedness (or, as the Hebrew has it more expressively, 'zemma', that is, incest) they have wrought in your midst. The more shameful parts of the father they have uncovered in you, and the uncleanness of the menstruous woman they have humbled in you; and each one has wrought abomination with his neighbor's wife, and the father-in-law has wickedly defiled his daughter-in-law; the brother has oppressed (or humbled) his sister, his father's daughter, in you. They have taken gifts in you to shed blood; usury and excess you have taken, and greedily you have falsely accused your neighbors (or and I will fill up the consummation of your malice in your oppression), and you have forgotten me, says the Lord God. Behold, I have clapped my hands over your avarice which you have practiced, and over the blood which has been shed in your midst. Will your heart endure, or will your hands prevail, in the days which I shall make for you? I the Lord have spoken and I will do it; and I will scatter you among the nations, and I will winnow you into the lands, and I will make your uncleanness fail from you; and I will possess you in the sight of the nations (or, according to the first edition of Aquila and Theodotion, and I will defile you; or, according to Symmachus, and I will wound you in the sight of the nations), and you shall know that I am the Lord. 'And you', he says, 'son of man — for I will use the word I am accustomed to use with you —, judge the city of bloods and show her all her abominations, so that she may know that she deservedly endures the imminent captivity and that by many bloods she has brought on the time of her ruin. First of all crimes, in place of God you have worshiped idols, and you have adored the works of your hands, and you have made the time of your years draw near, which for a long time was being announced and postponed, so that you might do penance. But according to your impenitent heart you treasure up wrath for yourself against the day of wrath. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all lands that are round about you, both near and far, which will triumph over you, or mock you, filthy, noble, great in ruin: filthy, because you have ceased to be clean; noble in evil, you who once surpassed all cities in nobility in good; great in ruin, so that the more lofty you were, the more heavily you should fall. And meanwhile, to pass over the rest, I will enumerate a few things that took place in you: your princes, judging not by righteousness but by the strength of their might and of their arm, shed innocent blood in you; others treated father and mother with insults, or cursed their parents, though Scripture says: Whoever curses father and mother shall die the death; the stranger and the sojourner they oppressed in your midst, as though sojourning and exile from their homeland were not enough for them in place of every distress; the orphan and the widow they grieved, or oppressed, in you, so that those whose whole protection lies in the justice of the laws were not only grieved but oppressed by you; my sanctuaries, or holy things, you despised, and my sabbaths you polluted, so that you did not distinguish between holy and polluted, between the day decreed for religion and the rest of the sabbath for the worship of God, and the other days on which it is permitted by the law to work and to serve the needs of the flesh; men who were 'detractors' — or, according to Symmachus and Theodotion, 'deceitful', which in the Hebrew is called 'rachil' — and murderers were in you, so as to blaspheme God or to do everything by deceit or violence; and they ate on the mountains, minding high things and lifted up against God in pride; wickedness, or incest, they wrought in your midst, so that what is rarely done even in corners and in secret, when the awareness of men is shunned by the wicked, this you did in the open — and what the incest is, the following passage indicates: They have laid bare the more shameful parts of the father in you, coupling with a stepmother against what is right and lawful, and they have humbled the uncleanness of the menstruous woman in you, not sparing nature nor granting a truce to their foulness, and neighing after their neighbor's wife; and, what is more wicked than this, the father-in-law burned for his daughter-in-law, and the brother knew nothing of a sister's rights, so as to violate a sister born not of the same womb but of the same father —; they took gifts so as to shed innocent blood; they turned the need of the poor into gain, so as to take usury and excess; and out of avarice they falsely accused their friends. This you have done', he says, 'O Jerusalem, because you have forgotten me; for the remembrance of God shuts out all shameful deeds. Hence I have taken on the bearing of the Lord in anger and have clapped my hands against your avarice and against the blood that has been shed in your midst, so that you may understand and recognize in your mind whether you can endure my wrath either in spirit or with your hands; for I the Lord have spoken and I will do it, so that, after you have been captured, Jerusalem, I will scatter you among the nations and winnow you into the air like useless chaff to be swept this way and that. And I am of such great clemency that my severity is turned into mercy; for I will do everything so that your uncleanness may fail from you and you may recover your former purity; and when you have recovered it, I will possess you in the sight of all the nations, so that, when you have been possessed by me, you may then understand that I myself am the Lord'. If, however, we follow the interpretation of Symmachus and Theodotion, of whom the one says: And I will wound you (or I will pierce you through), the other: I will defile you in the sight of the nations, everything must be referred to the bad sense, although what is said above is contrary to this sense: And I will make your uncleanness fail from you; for the failing of uncleanness is the restoration of purity. I have discussed both editions together, so as to avoid enlarging the books.

22:17-22

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, the house of Israel has been turned into dross for me; all these are bronze and tin and iron and lead in the midst of the furnace; they have become the dross of silver. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have all been turned into dross, therefore behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem, with a gathering of silver and bronze and iron and tin and lead into the midst of the furnace, so that I may kindle a fire in it for smelting: so will I gather in my fury and in my anger, and I will rest, and I will smelt you, and I will kindle you in the fire of my fury, and you shall be smelted in the midst of it. As silver is smelted in the midst of the furnace, so shall you be in the midst of it; and you shall know that I am the Lord; that I have poured out my indignation upon you. The Hebrew word 'sig' Symmachus translated 'dross', the first edition of Aquila and Theodotion στέμφυλον and γίγαρτον, both of which signify the 'pip' of the pressed grape; but the second translation of the same Aquila and the Seventy rendered it 'mixture'. Now dross denotes the filth and refuse of metals; and accordingly, with captivity near, nay, with the destruction of the city already impending, fire is applied so that, under the metaphor of smelting, pure silver may remain, which had been mixed with and corrupted by bronze, tin, iron and lead; of these, three — bronze, tin and lead — are of a fusible substance and are melted by fire, while iron is softened and thinned between anvil and hammer and takes various forms, according as the will of the craftsman may be. Just as, then, silver, which the metals mentioned above have corrupted, is put into the furnace so that, once the filth and the counterfeit substances have been removed, it may remain pure: 'so', he says, 'I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem and surround you with the Babylonian siege, so that I may kindle a fire in you for smelting; and what the immense heat of the flames does there, famine and pestilence do here, so that, after I have gathered you and kindled you in the fire of my fury, I may then rest and quell the pain of being despised by the vengeance of your punishments; and all this I will do so that, after I have poured out my indignation upon you, the end of your torment may be the knowledge of me, and you shall know that I am the Lord, the judge and requiter of all'. That he is said to be a smelter we read in many other places too, but above all in Malachi and Isaiah, of whom the one says: Behold, he says, the Lord enters like the fire of a smelter and like the herb of the washers, and he will sit smelting as gold and silver, and he will smelt the sons of Levi, the other: And the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and he will cleanse the blood from their midst by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning; and I think that this is also the sense of what is said in the Psalms: Prove me, O Lord, and try me, after which is added: Burn my reins and my heart, so that all the phlegm of the harmful humor in my loins may be dried up. What we have understood of Jerusalem, let us understand of the state of souls, which were created pure by God and received gold in understanding and wisdom, and silver in speech and eloquence, so that what they have conceived in the mind they may unfold in words. Of silver we read: The utterances of the Lord are chaste utterances, silver tried by fire, proved for the earth, purged sevenfold. Of gold and silver alike Psalm 67 (68) speaks, in which it is written: If you sleep in the midst of the lots, the wings of a dove covered with silver, and the hinder parts (or the inner parts) of her back in the greenness (or paleness) of gold. All indeed the glory of the king's daughter is within, she who speaks in the Song of Songs: The king has brought me into his chamber. Whoever has slept and rested between the two testaments at once takes up the silvered wings of the dove, and will shine with the brightness of gold in the treasury of the heart. To this sense, I think, those passages too are to be referred: that for sinners and for those who have deserved God's displeasure the heaven is bronze and the earth iron, and above all the land of Egypt, out of which the Lord leads Israel as out of an iron furnace; in Zechariah, too, iniquity sits upon a talent of lead, and in the song of Exodus it is said: They sank like lead in the most violent water; for they were pressed down by the heavy weight of their sins and could say: Like a heavy burden they have weighed heavily upon me. And just as the counterfeit likeness of bronze feigns the appearance of gold, so tin imitates the whiteness of silver, which the simple and rustic man does not easily tell apart. And it often happens that gold and silver, mixed with heretical depravity, are separated by the fire of the Holy Spirit in the judgment of the Lord, and the gold remains pure, and the silver of which the prophet says: I gave them gold and silver, but they made Baal out of them, to which this is similar: I brought them out with silver and gold, and there was not a feeble one among their tribes. And let the end of all punishments be to know that he himself is the Lord. A tin stone, or a mass of tin, we read in Zechariah too; what it signifies we have explained in its place.

22:23-31

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, say to her: You are a land unclean, and not rained upon in the day of fury. A conspiracy of prophets in her midst, like a lion roaring and seizing prey; they have devoured souls, they have taken wealth and price, they have multiplied her widows in her midst. Her priests have despised my law and have polluted my sanctuaries; between holy and profane they made no distinction, and between polluted and clean they did not discern, and from my sabbaths they turned away their eyes, and I was defiled in their midst. Her princes in her midst like wolves seizing prey, to shed blood and to destroy souls and greedily to pursue gains. And her prophets daubed them without tempering, seeing vain things and divining her falsehood, saying: Thus says the Lord God, when the Lord has not spoken. The people of the land they wronged with false accusation and plundered violently; the needy and the poor they afflicted, and the stranger they oppressed with false accusation without judgment. And I sought among them a man who would set up a wall and stand opposed against me for the land, so that I should not destroy it, and I did not find one. And I poured out my indignation upon them, in the fire of my anger I consumed them, I rendered their way upon their head, says the Lord God. A careful hearer might have asked what the dross was that violated the purity of the silver and mixed it with bronze, lead, tin and iron. What was expressed there, then, in the person of a city and a furnace is proclaimed here under the image of a land that has not been watered nor received rains — those rains of which it is written: I will command the clouds not to rain a shower upon it, the shower we await when the early and the late rain is given us, of which it is written: A voluntary rain you will set apart, O God, for your inheritance. And the day of fury is the one which each person procures for himself by the multitude of his sins. We wish to know what the dross of the city is, what the squalor of a land most hard and full of brambles and thorns. A conspiracy, he says, of prophets (or, according to the Seventy, of leaders) in her midst, who bear the likeness of a lion, of which Peter too writes: Our adversary the devil goes about like a roaring lion; and this lion and all his companions seek to devour not bodies but souls, and they take rewards and decide everything by money. That this happened to the people of the Jews at that time indeed, no one doubts; for because of the priests and the princes and the prophets the Lord brought evil upon them. But in our Jerusalem too we often see this: those who, according to the Seventy, devour souls in power and take a price, so as to make many widows who have lost the Lord, their bridegroom; and these prophets form a faction and a conspiracy, so as to be one another's supporters and to do everything for the sake of shameful gain; the priests, who ought to be the guardians of the temple and from whose mouth the knowledge of the law is sought, violate the sanctuaries and make no distinction between holy and profane except that of money; they turn their eyes away from the sabbaths and do not ponder the rest of God, which lies in the knowledge of the Scriptures, nor do they say with the prophet: Unveil my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law, nor that word of the Apostle: But we all with unveiled face behold the glory of the Lord. Among such prophets and priests the Lord, standing in their midst, is defiled, of whom it is written: In the midst of you stands one whom you do not know. The prophets, then, or leaders, are compared to lions; but the princes, whom we understand as men of a lower rank, imitate the rapine of wolves, so as to shed the blood not of bodies but of souls, and greedily pursue gains, by no means content with this: Those who serve the altar live by the altar, but, once they have come to the ministry of God, they amass the riches of Croesus. Her prophets also, who foretell things to come, daubed them without tempering — which we also discussed above, that of the soothsaying prophets who, without an admixture of chaff, plastered a wall that is broken down by the rains; men of this kind see vain things, and do not so much prophesy as divine falsehood, saying to the wretched land: 'Thus says the Lord, this he promises', when the Lord has not spoken to them; and the people of the land, being an imitator not of God at all but of the earthly works of the princes and priests, did everything through false accusation and power, oppressing not the rich but the poor, of whom it is written: But the poor man does not bear threatening, and: The ransom of a man's soul is his own riches; the stranger, too, and the sojourner, who had not yet become a citizen of the Church but was only a hearer, possessing the beginnings of faith, they oppressed with false accusation, so that, after one had gone around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, they made him a son of Gehenna. 'Amid such great', he says, 'vices and a multitude of crimes, I sought among them a man who could resist my anger and, after the pattern of Moses and Aaron and Samuel, set himself against my fire and my burning, and I could not find one — whence he said to Moses: Let me alone, and I will destroy this people —; and because I could not find one to resist me and hold me back, therefore I poured out all my indignation upon them and consumed them, not without measure and judgment, but so as to render their ways upon their own heads', either assigning to their authors the very sins they had committed, or surely upon the heads of the leader of the people, the prince and the prophets, of whom there was none who dared to resist the Lord in his anger, and on whose account the land, squalid and deserted, did not deserve to receive the rain of the Lord.

23:1-10

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt; in their youth they committed fornication: there their breasts were subdued, and the teats of their puberty were broken (or, as is contained in the Seventy, there their breasts fell, and there they were deflowered). Their names were Oholah the greater (or the elder) and Oholibah her sister; and I had them (or they became mine) and they bore sons and daughters: and their names were Samaria Oholah and Jerusalem Oholibah. Oholah therefore committed fornication over me; and she went mad (or went off) after her lovers, after the Assyrians, who drew near to her, clothed in hyacinth, princes and magistrates, young men of desire (or chosen), all horsemen, riders of horses. And she bestowed her fornications upon them, the chosen sons of the Assyrians, all of them; and in the uncleannesses (or inventions) of all those over whom she went mad she was polluted. Moreover she did not abandon her fornications either, which she had had in Egypt; for they too had slept with her in her youth, and had broken the breasts of her puberty (or and they themselves had deflowered her), and had poured out their fornication upon her. Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of Asshur, over whose lust she went mad; they uncovered her shame, they took her sons and daughters, and they killed her herself with the sword; and they became notorious women (or she became a byword among women), and they executed judgments (or vengeances) upon her. That the twelve tribes of Israel, which were joined together in Egypt, were afterwards divided into two and ten tribes and called Judah and Israel, the scripture of Kings and of Παραλιπόμενον [Chronicles] testifies. Over Judah there reigned, from the stock of David, Rehoboam son of Solomon, in Jerusalem, where the temple was, and the priests, and a great part of the tribe of Levi; but over the ten tribes, in Samaria, Jeroboam son of Nebat, of the tribe of Ephraim and of Joseph; of which Samaria is now called 'Oolla' [Oholah], which in our language sounds 'tabernacle', but Jerusalem 'Ooliba' [Oholibah], that is, 'my tabernacle in her'; for indeed among the ten tribes too there was a tabernacle, not of God but of idols: for Jeroboam, in order to turn the people away from the worship of God, had set up golden calves in Dan and Bethel. Let us speak, then, of each. These two women, Samaria and Jerusalem, were daughters of one mother, begotten of the stock of Israel, and they committed fornication in Egypt in their youth; for they would not, when led out of Egypt, have received on Mount Sinai the law forbidding them to venerate idols, had they not venerated the Egyptian monstrosities in Egypt —but the mother of both can be the Hittite, of whom we read above: Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite; and also when it is said: 'Let each one cast away the abominations of Egypt from his eyes', this signifies that Israel served idols in Egypt and that there the breasts of its virginity fell, or were broken — ; and Samaria is called the greater and the elder, either because of the multitude of the ten tribes, or because, after the death of Moses, Joshua son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, presided over the people, from which tribe too, we read, Jeroboam came, who split them off from the house of David. And God had them, or they became his, when they groaned under the works of Egypt, slaving before that at clay and brick; and afterwards they bore him sons and daughters, whether in the wilderness or in the land of promise. And first Oholah, that is, Samaria, committed fornication over God, when she went mad after the Assyrians, who were clothed in hyacinth, and not just anyone of the people but leaders and magistrates, not men worn out with age but all young men, chosen horsemen, whose idols she followed and from whom, against the command of God, she requested help; and they came and polluted her, so that she did not abandon whatever she had done in her youth in Egypt —for the Egyptians too had lain with her in her youth, whose images she venerated, and there she was deflowered and her breasts were broken; and so great was the abundance of fornication that they are said not to have committed fornication with her but to have poured out their fornication —. Therefore she was handed over to her lovers themselves, Pul and Tiglath-pileser and Shalmaneser, after whose lust she went mad; and they themselves uncovered her shame — τροπολογικῶς [tropologically], as of a harlot woman; but the uncovering of a city is captivity — ; and they led their sons and daughters captive and slaughtered her herself with the sword, so that she was butchered as an example to all women —and is celebrated, in the bad sense, in the talk of all of them — ; and they executed judgments and vengeances upon her —so as to leave nothing of safety in her, but the ten tribes are held in captivity to this day in the mountains and cities of the Medes to which they were transported —. According to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], we have discussed more fully in the prophet Hosea what Joseph, Ephraim, Samaria, Jezreel and Israel signify, and how they are opposed to the house of David and to Jerusalem, which signifies the Church — of whom Psalm 77 (78) also sounds: The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, turned back in the day of battle, and again: He rejected the tabernacle of Joseph and chose the tribe of Judah; for the Lord chose the house of confession, the Church, and rejected the tabernacle of 'Joseph', which means 'increase'; and they, setting aside the law of God, added golden calves of their own worship —; and she is called 'Oolla', that is, 'tabernacle', not of God but of error and of demons; and the sister, greater and elder because of her multitude and her captivity by the Assyrians, committed fornication against God, because she abandoned the truth of the faith and went mad after the princes of the heretics, her lovers, who were clothed in hyacinth, promising themselves lofty and heavenly things, and riders, of whom it is said: Some in chariots and some on horses, chosen sons of the Assyrians, and leaders and magistrates, who promise themselves knowledge and eloquence; and she did this because the same fornications that she had had in Egypt, that is, before she believed and while she was still living in the world, she practiced in heresy too; and she was deflowered by Assyrian men, who persevere in malice, or by avengers — for our adversary the devil is himself the enemy and the avenger — ; they broke the breasts of Samaria, and destroyed the virginity which she had had in the Church; therefore she was handed over to her lovers, according to the Apostle, who writes: I delivered them to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme, and he delivered them for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved; they uncovered the shame of wretched Samaria, and displayed all her foulness; and her sons and daughters, who were begotten of her, both those endowed with knowledge and the simple and unskilled, they led captive; and they killed her herself with the spiritual sword; and they are celebrated, in the bad sense, in the talk of the whole world; and they become notorious among all the doctrines of the world, so that her foulness is punished as an example to all women.

23:11-21

And when her sister Oholibah had seen this, she went mad with lust more than she, and shamelessly offered her fornication, beyond the fornication of her sister, to the sons of the Assyrians: to leaders and magistrates coming to her, clothed in varied garments (or costly), to horsemen who rode upon horses, and to youths all of outstanding form. And I saw that she was polluted: one way for both; and she increased her fornications. And when she had seen men painted on the wall, images of the Chaldeans expressed in colors, with their loins girded with belts, and dyed tiaras on their heads, with the appearance of all leaders (or of all the tristatae), in the likeness of the sons of Babylon and of the land of the Chaldeans in which they were born, she went mad over them with the lust of her eyes, and sent messengers to them in Chaldea. And when the sons of Babylon had come to her, to the bed of breasts (or of those turning aside), they polluted her with their debaucheries; and she was polluted by them, and her soul was sated (or withdrew) from them. And she laid bare her fornications, and uncovered her shame; and my soul withdrew from her, as my soul had withdrawn from her sister. For she multiplied her fornications, remembering the days of her youth in which she committed fornication in the land of Egypt; and she went mad with lust over the bedding of those whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses (or whose private parts are like the private parts of horses). And you revisited the wickedness of your youth, when your breasts were subdued in Egypt, and the teats of your puberty were broken. According to the letter the interpretation is easy: that Oholibah —that is, Jerusalem, in which was the tabernacle of God —, seeing the blows dealt to her sister, was not warned by the example to draw back her foot from error, but increased her sister's fornication —for that one fabricated idols once, and outside, in Dan and Bethel; but this one often, on the high places and in the temple of God, worshiped the statue of Baal and committed fornication with the Assyrians; for the idol Baal, or Bel, and, to speak more plainly, Belis, the religion of the Assyrians, was consecrated by Ninus son of Belus in honor of his father — ; and she shamelessly offered her fornication to the Assyrians, to leaders and magistrates who were clothed in varied and many-colored garments, to horsemen and youths all of outstanding form, so that the fornication of both sisters became one. But Jerusalem increased her fornications in this, that, seeing on the walls images of the Chaldeans, she went mad with lust and, deceived by their form and dress, sent messengers to them requesting help, and they came and polluted her. And because pleasure is not perpetual but quickly brings satiety, polluted and sated with them, she withdrew from their covenant. 'Therefore I too, seeing her foul deeds and fornications made public to all, withdrew from her, so that she who had outdone her sister's crimes might also surpass her sister in the magnitude of her punishments'. She was of such wantonness that she committed all the errors of her youth at an age already more mature, and pursued the Egyptian vices in her lust for the Chaldeans too; for she once went mad in her bedding with the Egyptians, whose flesh is in the likeness of asses, with so copious an issue of seed, or private parts so huge, that they surpass the deformity of horses. 'Nor did the wickedness of her youth cease; rather, she went back to it after she became mine, so that both in the wilderness and in the land of promise she sighed for the old lust in which she was deflowered and her breasts were broken and all her virginal beauty perished'. Moreover, according to tropology the understanding is difficult: how the Church can surpass heretical lust; unless perhaps we can say this, that the servant who knows the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten with many blows, and that heretics commit abominations outside and perish by shipwreck outside the ark of Noah, while churchmen, if, though following the true faith, they imitate Assyrian and Chaldean vices and follow the many-colored images of sins, deserve greater torments — or do we not send messengers to the 'Chaldeans', which means 'as it were demons', when we lay open and offer them the breasts to be broken in the bosom, where the lodging of the mind is, and, sated with pleasures, pass from some women to others; and desire not so much fornication as a number of harlots; and come to such madness that, after long years of the Lord's service, we return to Egypt and do the things we did in the world before we received the name of the faith? —.

23:22-27

Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stir up all your lovers against you, with whom your soul was sated; and I will gather them against you round about, the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles and tyrants and princes, all the sons of the Assyrians, youths of outstanding form, all the leaders and magistrates, princes of princes, and renowned riders of horses; and they will come upon you equipped with chariot and wheel, a multitude of peoples: with breastplate and shield and helmet they will be armed against you on every side, and I will set judgment before them, and they will judge you with their judgments. And I will set my jealousy in you, which they exercise with you in fury: they will cut off your nose and your ears, and what remains they will cut down with the sword; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters, and your last will be devoured by fire. And they will strip you of your garments, and take away the vessels of your glory; and they will make your wickedness rest from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt, and you will not lift up your eyes to them, and you will not remember Egypt any more. (LXX: "Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stir up your lovers against you, from whom your soul withdrew; and I will bring them against you round about, the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, Facud and Sue and Cue, and all the sons of the Assyrians with them, chosen youths, all leaders and magistrates, τριστάτας [tristatae, high officers], and renowned men riding on horses; all will come upon you from the north, chariots and wheels with a multitude of peoples: shields and targes, and they will set a guard upon you round about, and I will set judgment before their face, and they will judge you with their judgments. And I will set my jealousy in you, and they will deal with you in the wrath of fury: they will take away your nose and your ears, and your remnant they will cast down with the sword; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters, and fire will devour your residue. And they will strip you of your garment, and take up the vessels of your boasting; and they will turn away your impieties from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt, and you will not raise your eyes to them, and you will not remember Egypt any more.") 'Because you remembered the flesh of the Egyptians and imitated the foulness of an unclean nation which venerates images of all the beasts, therefore I will bring against you your lovers, sated with whose embrace you withdrew from their covenant, so that, as great as your love had been before, into so great a hatred you might be turned. The sons, I say, of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, nobles, tyrants and princes — in place of which the Hebrew has 'facud' and 'sue' and 'cue', which many understand as nations of the east, since we find names of this kind neither in the volume of Kings nor in Chronicles, nor even in Jeremiah, which describe the captivity of Jerusalem, nor in any other place of holy scripture; nor is it surprising if the Seventy set down the Hebrew names themselves, since Symmachus too and Theodotion agree in the same words — ; all', he says, 'the Assyrians, horsemen and youths of outstanding form, leaders and magistrates — or τριστάτας, which we have translated 'princes of princes', of whom we also read in Exodus: Chosen riders, τριστάτας, in place of which Latin simplicity translated 'ternos stratores' [grooms by threes]; and 'tristatae' is the name among the Hebrews for the second rank after the royal dignity, of whom it is written: Yet he did not attain to the first three; they were princes of the cavalry and the infantry and of the tributes, whom we call magistrates of both services and prefects of the grain office — ; all', he says, 'in chariots and on horses, armed with breastplate, helmet and shield, will besiege you, and that round about; and I will give them judgment, so that you may be judged by those whom you had left and whose pact you had made void; and they will judge you with their judgments as an adulteress; and I will set', he says, 'my jealousy in you, which they exercise with you in fury — for my jealousy over faith not kept is present even among enemies — : your nose', he says, 'and your ears they will cut off — as of an adulteress caught in debauchery — so that, disfigured, you may cease to please — for just as in the face all the beauty of the countenance consists in the comeliness of the nostrils and in the ears, from which in women pearls and gems hang down, so the dignity of the king and of the judges, which is signified in the face and the ears, will be cut off by their sword — ; they themselves will take your sons and your daughters — yours, he says, and yours, not mine and mine, because they were begotten of adultery —, and the rest will be devoured by fire; and they will strip', he says, 'you of your garments, with which I had adorned you, and of the vessels of your glory, of gold and silver, which I had granted you for the ceremonies of the temple — of which it is written: I gave them gold and silver, and they made them for Baal — ; and I will do all these things so that, your beauty lost and your bewitching face disfigured, your wickedness may at last rest, and the fornication which you learned and practiced in Egypt, so that, after you have lost your nose and ears, you may by no means dare to lift your eyes to the Chaldeans and show your hideousness to your former lovers; nor may you any longer remember the lust of the Egyptians, in the size of whose flesh you delighted'. All of this is said under the metaphor of an adulteress, disfigured because of her adultery, so that she may no longer glory in her comeliness but blush in the hideousness which she has merited by the magnitude of her pleasures. Whatever is said τροπικῶς [figuratively] of Jerusalem can also be referred to the soul, which, joined by its virtues to the embrace of God, afterwards turned adulteress to vices and withdrew from him, and, all her crimes being laid open, was stripped and disfigured and shown to all, so that she may at some time desist from her wickedness; and may not glory in the dignity of her name, but, from her consciousness of evil and her remembrance of Egypt, may not dare any longer to lift her eyes to heaven; whence too her nose is cut off and her ears are amputated, because she had turned the odor of good fragrance into stench and had heard the judgment of blood; and this we understand not only of smell and hearing but of sight too, of which Samson and Zedekiah are deprived because they had abused it; God also makes deaf and mute, so that their tongue may not pass through to the earth; and all touch is taken away in those who have utterly lost life. And these things will happen so that all things may be purged by fire, and the fornication of Egypt may perish, and she may no longer be able to raise her eyes to evils.

23:28-35

For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hated, into the hands with which your soul was sated, and they will deal with you in hatred, and take away all your labors, and leave you naked and full of disgrace. Your wickedness and your fornications have done these things to you, because you committed fornication after the nations, among whom you were polluted in their idols. You walked in the way of your sister, and I will give her cup into your hand. Thus says the Lord God: You will drink the cup of your sister, deep and wide — you will be for derision and for scorn: you who are most capacious, you will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow! —, and the cup of grief and sadness, the cup of your sister Samaria; and you will drink it and drain it to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, and you will tear your breasts (or, as the Seventy translated, I will take away her feasts and new moons), for I have spoken, says the Lord. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have forgotten me, and cast me behind your body, you too bear your wickedness and your fornications. It is profitable for Jerusalem too to have enmity against the Assyrians and Chaldeans and by no means to remember Egypt, but to be delivered into the hands of those who hated her, to be punished; and she is not delivered to them before her soul has been sated with them, so that, after she has repented of her old sins, she may then be purged by punishments, and lose all the labors which she acquired by the harlot's art, and see her nakedness and disgrace, and know that it was not the Lord who did all these things to her but her own fornications, by which she committed fornication among the nations, which he enumerated above, so as to worship their images. 'In the ways', he says, 'of your sister Samaria you walked; therefore you must drink the cup of her whose sins you followed — and that a cup is often taken for punishments and torments, there are many examples, among which is this: A cup in the hand of the Lord, full of pure wine, mixed. And he has tilted it from this; yet its dregs are not emptied: all the sinners of the earth shall drink; and in Isaiah it is called 'the cup of ruin' and 'the draught of fury'; and God speaks to Jeremiah, saying: Take the cup of pure wine from my hand, and you shall give drink to all the nations to which I shall send you; and they shall drink and vomit, and go mad; for just as certain cathartics are given so that the noxious humor that is in bodies may be purged out, so the Lord too gives a most undiluted cup of torments, to take away from sinners whatever there is of gall and bitterness and restore them to their former health — ; and the cup itself will be deep and wide: deep in the magnitude of the punishments, wide in the length of the captivity; but when', he says, 'you have been made drunk and seized by sorrow, and have drunk the cup to the dregs and drained it to such a degree that you devour even the fragments of the cup itself, then you will be weary of your former fornication and will tear the breasts which had been broken in Egypt and which were subdued and crushed by your lovers — or I will take away all your feasts and new moons, so that in place of solemnity and gladness you may have eternal lamentation and grief —. Since, therefore, you have done these things and forgotten me and cast me behind your body —or backward, because of the vices of the body, or behind the genitals, by which the foulness of turpitude is indicated —, therefore bear your wickedness and your impiety — that is, the punishments which you have merited by your impiety and crimes —'. This that is said: And you will drink to the dregs; and you will devour its fragments, can be understood meaningfully of Jerusalem, which drank the cup of her sister Samaria last, and drained, as it were, the dregs of her torments to the bottom.

23:36-49

And the Lord spoke to me, saying: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah, and declare to them their crimes (or iniquities)? For they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands, and they have committed fornication with their idols (or inventions); moreover their sons too, whom they had borne to me, they offered to them to be devoured (or they led through the fire). But this too they did to me: they polluted my sanctuary on that day, and profaned my sabbaths. And when they sacrificed their sons to their idols, and entered my sanctuary on that day to pollute it, these things too they did in the midst of my house. They sent to men coming from afar, to whom they had sent a messenger; and so, behold, they came. For them you washed yourself (or when they had come, at once you bathed), and painted round your eyes with stibium, and adorned yourself with womanly finery; you sat on a beautiful couch, and a table was adorned before you; my incense and my ointment (or oil) you set upon it. And the voice of an exulting multitude was in her (or and with a composed voice she leapt about), and among the men, indeed, multitudes of people were brought and came from the desert (or drunk from the desert); they put bracelets on their hands and most beautiful crowns on their heads. And I said to her who is worn down in adultery: Now she too will commit fornication in her fornication. And they went in to her as to a harlot woman; so they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, wicked women (or to work iniquity). Righteous men, then, are they; these will judge them with the judgment of adulteresses and the judgment of those who shed blood, because they have committed adultery and blood is on their hands. For thus says the Lord God: Bring a multitude against them, and deliver them to tumult and to plunder; and let them be stoned with the stones of the peoples, and pierced with their swords; they will kill their sons and daughters, and burn their houses with fire. And I will remove wickedness (or impiety) from the land, and all women will learn not to act according to their wickedness (or impiety); and they will lay your wickedness (or impiety) upon you, and you will bear the sins of your idols, and you will know that I am the Lord God. As I have often pointed out, the small points in which the edition of the Seventy differs from the Hebrew I have joined on at the side, providing against the reader's distaste. Now it followed that he who had described the adulteries of Samaria and Jerusalem separately should announce their punishments together. And everything is said as to adulteresses, and, after a ἀνακεφαλαιῶσι [recapitulation] has been made, their crimes are briefly set forth, so that, rightly, according to the command of the law, the stoning of the people may follow upon the adulteresses. 'Since, therefore, they are adulteresses, pronounce a just sentence; for they have committed adultery with idols, and blood is on their hands, the blood, namely, of those whom they sacrificed to idols, so as to consecrate to demons the sons whom they had borne to me; nor did they do this outside, and on the mountains and in the groves, as they had often been accustomed to do, but at the last they polluted my temple, so as to set the statue of Baal in it; and they profaned my sabbaths, so that the religion neither of place nor of time was kept among them. But neither were they content only with present adulteries, nor did it suffice them that, after sacrificing my sons, they made them their idols' or the demons', but, wanton also in foreign pleasures, they venerated the images of the Assyrians and Chaldeans. And when these had come, Oholibah, Jerusalem, you fulfilled for them the whole bearing of an adulteress: you washed your body, smeared your eyes with stibium, put on womanly adornment, sat on a couch prepared for lust, set out feasts with which to restore the strength of your lovers, broken by lust; my incense and ointment — which I had ordered to be made specially for me, and that soul to be exterminated from the people which wished to make it for private uses — you offered to idols, so as to gather a throng of peoples, or sang with every kind of musician, so as to please your lovers not only by sight but by hearing and smell and all the senses; and they came to you drunk, not with any urbane elegance, but from the desert and the wilderness, displaying the bearing of rustics and brigands. And into such madness of pleasures did you burn, O most wicked sisters, that you placed your bracelets and hair-ornaments upon the hands and heads of your lovers, or upon yourselves, so that, full of adornment, you might be disgraced. Wherefore I said to her, whether to Jerusalem or to Samaria or to both: So have you worn down your brow that you are by no means polluted in secret, nor do you heed the gaze either of a husband or of men, but like harlots you are prostituted publicly; they went in to you as to harlots, vying with one another in their desire to pollute you. I will therefore deliver you for punishment to those to whom you delivered yourselves of your own accord for defilement; for they are righteous men in this, that at my command they torment the adulteress and parricide. For thus says the Lord God: By the warning of your voice, O prophet, gather against them a multitude of peoples, and first let all their substance be plundered; then let them be stoned and pierced with swords; and let their sons and daughters be slaughtered, and their houses burn. And all these things will be done so that impiety may be removed from the land, and all women and all provinces may learn from their punishments to avoid the like, so that, after you have received what you deserve and have borne the crimes of your idols, you may then know that I am the Lord'. All these things were said τροπικῶς [figuratively] and under the type of adulteresses against Samaria and Jerusalem: that, delivered to the Assyrians and Chaldeans, they were led into captivity and their cities were burned up in fire, and the peoples were killed who had venerated the images of demons in place of God. These things can also be understood of the time after the coming of Christ: that righteous men from the peoples of the Gentiles, they themselves, judge the Samaritans and the Jews by comparison with themselves and deliver them to be devoured, those to whom the Lord had said: Your house will be left to you desolate, and: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, know that its desolation draws near; for to this day they are adulteresses and are crushed by the stones of the whole world, because they sent messengers to those who were far off and could not say: I am the Lord who draws near, and not from afar, says the Lord; and they prepared themselves for their lovers, the demons, and all the adornment and finery which they had received from God as a natural good they turned into the worship of demons, and their works and comeliness, which we understand in the bracelets and the diadem, they offered to their adulterous lovers; and their punishment is a fear to the Gentiles, or rather to those of the Gentiles who have believed, lest they suffer the like if they do what Samaria and Jerusalem did. From them impieties will be taken away then, when they have received their crimes and have taken away from their eyes the veil that is placed before the face of Moses, so that they may know that he himself is the Lord Jesus Christ, whom they denied to be the Son of God.

24:1-14

And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying: Son of man, write down for yourself the name of this day, on which the king of Babylon has been made strong against Jerusalem today. And you shall speak by a proverb a parable to the provoking house, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the pot; set it on, I say, and put water into it. Heap its pieces into it, every good part, the thigh and the shoulder, choice pieces and full of bones; take the fattest of the flock, and arrange also piles of bones under it. Its cooking has boiled up, and its bones have been boiled through in the midst of it. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloods, to the pot whose rust is in it, and its rust has not gone out of it. Piece by piece, and by its pieces, cast it out; the lot has not fallen upon it, for its blood is in the midst of it; upon a most clear rock she poured it out; she did not pour it out upon the ground, so that it could be covered with dust: that I might bring my indignation upon her and avenge with vengeance, I have set her blood upon the most clear rock, so that it should not be covered. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloods, whose pyre I will make great. Heap up the bones, which I will set alight with fire; the flesh shall be consumed, and the whole composition shall be boiled down, and the bones shall waste away. Set it also empty upon the live coals, that it may grow hot, and its bronze may melt, and its defilement may be melted down in its midst, and its rust may be consumed. With much labor there has been sweating, and its excessive rust has not gone out of it, not even through fire. Your uncleanness is execrable, because I wished to cleanse you, and you were not cleansed of your filth; but neither will you be cleansed before I make my indignation rest upon you. I the Lord have spoken; it comes, and I will do it: I will not pass over, nor spare, nor be appeased. According to your ways and according to your devices I have judged you, says the Lord. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying: Son of man, write down for yourself the day from this day on which the king of Babylon set himself firmly over Jerusalem from this present day. And speak a parable to the exasperating house, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the cauldron, and pour water upon it.
