But if we wish, following the prophecy of Hosea, which is almost wholly directed to the ten tribes, that is, to Joseph and Ephraim and Samaria and Israel, to understand the knowledge falsely so called and the various crowds of heretics, we shall say this: that in the last time, when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in and all Israel has been saved, then the hostile peoples also, who fought against the house of Judah and the confession of the Church, will give themselves up to the faith of the Church, and, having abandoned all their errors and the princes of this world who are being destroyed and their own patriarchs who led them down into the abyss of blasphemies, they will rise up, and leave their idols and their abominations which they had fashioned out of their own heart, and from all their dwelling places in which they sinned will pass over to the faith of the Church, and be cleansed, and be the people of Christ, and he will be their God; which I know I have dictated more fully on the prophet Hosea. But if the Jews and judaizing Christians wish to refer these things to the reign of a thousand years, they will be compelled by necessity to accept that all who have been saved will dwell in the land of Israel, that Jerusalem is to be built, the temple to be erected, all the ceremonies of the law to be practiced, the sabbath to be observed, the injury of circumcision to be received, that there is to be eating and drinking, and that an abundance of riches is to be esteemed as the highest blessedness and all wealth, when the Apostle says: Food for the belly and the belly for foods: but God will destroy both it and them; but just as, in the type of the resurrection, the preceding prophetic word showed the restoration of the Jewish people, not carnal but spiritual, so also this prophecy pertains not at all to the happiness of the flesh but to that of the soul, and to the faith of Christ, by which we are cleansed in baptism, whose kingdom is for ever, so that we may not await as things to come what has already been accomplished and what we know is accomplished daily.

38:1-23

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Gog and the land of Magog, the prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy concerning him, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, the prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal, and I will turn you about, and I will put a bridle in your jaws, and I will lead out (or I will gather) both you and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed with breastplates, a great multitude seizing spear and shield and sword (or bucklers and helmets and swords). Persians and Ethiopians and Libyans with them, all with shields and helmets; Gomer and all its troops, the house of Togarmah, the sides of the north (or from the farthest parts of the north) and all its strength, and many peoples (or nations) with you. Prepare and equip yourself and all your multitude that is heaped together to you, and be for them a command (or and you shall be to me for a guard). After many days you will be visited; in the last of the years you will come to the land which has turned back (or been perverted) from the sword and has been gathered out of many peoples to the mountain (or land) of Israel, which had been continually deserted: this one has been led out from the peoples, and all of them will dwell confidently. And going up you will come like a storm and like a cloud, to cover the land, you and all your troops and many peoples (or nations) with you. Thus says the Lord God: On that day words will go up according to your heart, and you will think a most wicked thought, and you will say: I will go up to the land (or upon the land) without a wall (or cast off), I will come to those who are at rest and dwell securely (or in peace); all of them dwell without a wall, they have no bars and gates; to seize spoils and fall upon plunder, and to lay your hand upon those who had been deserted and were afterwards restored, and upon the people which has been gathered out of the nations, which has begun to possess and to be the inhabitant of the navel of the earth. Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish (or the Carthaginians) and all its lions (or villages) will say to you: Is it to take spoils that you come? Behold, to seize plunder you have gathered your multitude, to carry off silver and gold, to take away household goods and property, and to seize boundless booty. Therefore prophesy, son of man, and you shall say to Gog: Thus says the Lord God: Will you not, on that day when the people Israel dwells confidently (or in peace), know (or rise up)? And you will come from your place from the sides (or from the farthest parts) of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riders of horses, a great company and a mighty army. And you will go up against my people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. In the last days you will be (or it will be), and I will bring you upon my land, so that all the nations may know me, when I am sanctified in you before their eyes, O Gog. Thus says the Lord God: You then are he of whom I spoke in ancient days, by the hand of my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days and times (or years), that I would bring you upon them. And it shall be on that day, on the day of the coming of Gog upon the land of Israel, says the Lord God, that my indignation will go up in my fury. And in my zeal, in the fire of my wrath I have spoken, that on that day there shall be a great commotion upon the land of Israel, and the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field (or of the plain), and every creeping thing that moves upon the ground, and all the men who are upon the face of the earth shall be moved before my face; and the mountains shall be overturned (or split) and the enclosure walls shall fall (or the valleys), and every wall shall collapse to the ground. And I will call together against him on all my mountains a sword (or every terror of the sword), says the Lord God; the sword of each one (or of each man) shall be directed against his brother. And I will judge him with pestilence (or death) and blood and violent rain and immense stones (or of hail); fire and sulphur I will rain upon him, and upon his army (or upon all who are with him), and upon the many peoples who are with him, and I will be magnified and sanctified and I will be known in the sight of many nations, and they shall know that I am the Lord. First the foundations of the history must be laid, and it must be known that this is the last word of the Lord to the prophet Ezekiel; for after it we cannot in any way find anything similar, except what is written in the twenty-fifth year of the exile of Jeconiah: The hand of the Lord came upon me, and brought me there, that is, into the land of Israel, when the building of the temple is described and the order of its ceremonies is related. Next it must be observed that the face of the prophet is set, or made firm, against Gog the land, or of the land, of Magog; for there is need of firmness and of much consideration of the countenance, so that we may be able to know the things that are said, according to that apostolic saying: But we all, contemplating the glory of the Lord with unveiled face, are re-formed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord. Accordingly the Jews and our own Judaizers think that Gog is the Scythian nations, savage and innumerable, which stretch beyond the Caucasus mountain and the Maeotic marsh and near the Caspian Sea as far as India — and that these are to be stirred up by the devil after the reign of a thousand years —, and that they are to come into the land of Israel to fight against the saints, with many nations gathered together with them: first Meshech, whom Josephus interprets as the Cappadocians; then Tubal, whom the same man supposes to be the Iberians or Spaniards, and the Hebrews the Italians, having with them in their army Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans; also Gomer and Togarmah, whom they interpret as the Galatians and Phrygians; also the Sabaeans and Dedan and the Carthaginians, or Tarshish; and that this is what John too sets down in his Revelation: And when the thousand years are finished, Satan will be loosed from his prison, and he will go out to seduce the nations in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for war: whose number is as the sand of the sea. And they went up over the breadth of the earth, and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. And fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them; and the devil who seduced them was cast into the lake of fire and sulphur, where the beast and the false prophet were, and they will be tormented day and night for ages of ages; not understanding that the whole volume of John, which is headed with the title of Revelation, is mystical, and that we need revelation so that we may be able to say with the prophet: Unveil my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law. Others, however, abandoning the earthly sense and the Jewish and old-wives' fables, which are harmful and drag down into the depths those who acquiesce in them, climb up too far to the heights and invent much worse trifles, so that they describe the wars of the devil and of all his army in the heavenly Jerusalem, and under the ἐτυμολογίαις [etymologies] of the individual nations interpret the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. Leaving all these things to the reader's judgment, we shall try not so much to condemn the views of others as to affirm the Church's explanation. 'Gog' is called in the Greek tongue δῶμα, in the Latin 'roof'; 'Magog', moreover, means 'from the roof' — so all pride, and the knowledge falsely so called which raises itself against the knowledge of the truth, is shown by these names —; these are the roofs of which Isaiah too speaks in the vision against the valley of Zion: What has happened to you now, that you all go up onto the empty roofs?; and by 'roof' we shall interpret the princes of the heretics, and by 'from the roof' those who have taken up their doctrines; and fittingly, after the many mystical prophecies in this volume, the last prophecy is against Gog and Magog — for if It is the time of judgment, according to Peter, that it should begin from the house of God, and according to this same Ezekiel, who says: And begin from my saints, and: The last enemy, death, is destroyed, in Isaiah too the first word is directed against Judea, in which is the confession of the Lord, and the last against the four-footed beasts which are in the desert; rightly here too the last word is directed against Gog and Magog, who assail the city of God, which the rush of the river makes glad, and which says in Isaiah: I am a strong city which is besieged, and of which it is written in the Gospel: A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden, and more fully in the psalm: Jerusalem, which is built as a city whose sharing of it is in the selfsame. Mountains are round about it, and the Lord is round about his people —. Moreover, as to the fact that in the army of Gog or Magog, who according to the Seventy, Symmachus and Theodotion is prince of Ros, Meshech and Tubal, Aquila translates the first nation, 'Ros', as 'head', and we too have followed him — so that the sense is: The prince of the head of Meshech and Tubal; and in truth neither in Genesis, nor in any other place of Scripture, nor even in Josephus, who in the first book of the Antiquities sets out the names of all the Hebrew nations, have we been able to find this nation, from which it is clear that 'Ros' signifies not 'a nation' but 'head'; this too must be briefly noted, that in Ezekiel Gog is said to be the prince of the land of Magog, whereas Revelation records that both Gog and Magog are nations which go out from the four corners of the earth; and that just as from Jacob, who was afterwards called Israel, the whole people of the Hebrews received the name Israel, and from Aram Syria, from Mesraim Egypt, whose names are written in Genesis, so too from the prince Gog all who are subject to him are called Magog —; 'Mosoch', however, means 'madness', and 'Thubal' 'whole' or 'all things': so the 'prince' and 'head of proud madness and of all evils' — according to what is written: The world is set in the evil one — are called 'Gog' and 'Magog' — nations which, hostile and adverse to the saints, go out from the corners of the earth, abandoning the straight line and the arrangement of the camps of God which is related in Numbers, and not knowing that testimony: Many will come from the east and the west and the north and the south, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of God, and in another place: I will say to the north: Bring; and to the south-west wind: Do not hinder, bring my sons from a distant land and my daughters from the end of the earth, all who are called by my name; but not such are the corners of the earth from which Gog and Magog go out: beside such corners the harlot stands in Proverbs, who hastens to deceive the foolish young men passing by through the streets, that is, through the broad and spacious way which leads to death: the scribes and Pharisees too pray at the corners of the streets so as to be seen by men, who have received their reward —. What, then, is the threat against Gog? 'I will turn you about (or I will convert), and I will put a bridle in your jaws: first I will make you waver from your opinion and be converted, and I will put a bridle in your jaws — of which it is written: With bridle and bit bind fast the jaws of those who do not draw near to you —, so that the untamed horse, wanton and rushing headlong over precipices, may be subjected to the bridle of the Lord' — to whom the prophet says: You will mount upon your horses, and your riding is salvation, and to Job it is said through clouds and whirlwind: Did you surround the horse with strength? Such were the horses and horsemen whose multitude John saw in heaven —. So he says to Gog: I will lead out (or I will gather) you and all the army (or strength) of yours; he who is led out and gathered from dispersion is drawn back to salvation — according to what is promised in the law: If your dispersion be from the height of heaven to its height, from there I will gather you —. Of his horses too, and horsemen clothed with breastplates — who imitate the armor of the Apostle and boast that they have the breastplates of righteousness — there is an excessive multitude, and all of them seize shield and sword against the Church, and they are most savage nations, hostile to Israel: Persians, Ethiopians and Libyans — whose wars against the people of God are related in the holy Scriptures —; Gomer too and the house of Togarmah, who come from the sides of the 'north' — which is a most cold wind and is called by the name 'dexter' [right-hand] —, and all the strength of Magog and all the peoples that are subject to him, will come with him to battle. To him it is said by way of εἰρωνείαν [irony]: 'Prepare and equip yourself, and heap together to yourself all your multitude, which obeys your commands; but know that after many days you will be visited' — according to what is written: I will visit their iniquities with the rod and their sins with stripes —. 'In the last', he says, 'of the years you will come'; whence John too says: My little children, it is the last hour, and the people of the Gentiles is hired at the eleventh hour to work in the vineyard; to whose land — that is, the land of the meek and the land of the saints, which brings forth fruit a hundredfold and sixtyfold and thirtyfold — Gog comes to storm it, the land which has turned back, or turned away, from the sword — for it knows that it is written: Scatter, O Lord, the nations that desire wars —, and abides in peace, and has been gathered from many peoples and nations so that, having despised the error of the nations, it might come to the mountains of Israel, that is, the patriarchs and prophets, who were once continually deserted, without the law and the precepts of God, to which it is afterwards said: More are the children of the deserted one than of her who has a husband; these are the deserted and waterless places in which the devil could find no place, because they had been called to salvation, and afterwards, taking with him seven other demons more wicked than himself, he returned to his house, that is, to the nation of Israel. This, he says, has been led out from the peoples, land being understood, or: This one has been led out from the nations, so that the people of believers may be understood, which has dwelt in peace; and it trusts in the Lord. And Gog, going up with all his army, will come like a storm and like a cloud, to cover the land of the believers — for which of the heretics, whose prince is the devil, does not come like a storm against the Church, and hasten to overwhelm and cover with the cloud of his words all the simple among the believers? —; whence it is said to him: 'As far as lies in you, you will cover all things, you and all your troops and many peoples with you'; and fittingly Gog, going up, has no willing rain, no early and late shower to gladden the parched fields, but storm and darkness, so as to confound all things with gloom and error. Therefore the Lord God speaks these things to him: At that time, that is, in the last days, words will go up upon your heart, and you will think a most wicked thought — as Scripture says: If the spirit of one who has power should wish to go up upon you, do not abandon your place; but on the contrary God goes up into the heart of the holy man, of whom it is written: He has set ascents in his heart —; and Gog says: I will go up to the land without a wall (or cast forth) — that is, the land which is destitute of the help of God and not fortified by the argumentation of the dialecticians, I will come to those who are at rest, dwelling securely (or in peace) — for our king is peaceable, and his place is in peace —; all of them, he says, dwell without a wall, they have no bars and gates. This the devil, the prince of the heretics, says: that the Church has no fortifications, nor the worldly wisdom which is foolishness with God, so that he may seize the spoils and fall upon the plunder of the Church, and lay his hand upon those who had been deserted when they did not have the knowledge of God and afterwards, restored through Christ, come to the Father — he says in the Gospel: Father, I have revealed your name to men —; and so that we may know that the people which had been deserted and afterwards restored signifies the Christian people, there follows: And upon the people which has been gathered out of the nations, which people has begun to possess the inheritance of Christ and to be the inhabitant of the navel of the earth — of which it is written: He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth. Truth, indeed, has sprung from the earth; which says in the Gospel: I am the way and the truth and the life —. While he thinks and says these things and hastens to snatch the possession of the Church, the nations which had been converted from their former error to salvation: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish — of Carthage or of the sea — who amid the waves of this world seek merchandise by good works, and all their villages or lions — or lions' whelps, as is contained in the Hebrew —, will say to him what follows — that the Seventy and Theodotion, however, put 'villages' in place of 'lions' whelps', which in Hebrew are called 'chaphir', is an evident error: for if you write it with the letter 'chi', it is called 'lion's whelp', but if with 'ce', which in Hebrew is called 'coph', it is called 'field' and 'village'; whence Capharnaum too is called 'most beautiful field' —. So Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish will say, and all the saints who are called lions' whelps, or at any rate the villages and dwellings of the believers: 'O Gog, is it for this that you come: to snatch the spoils of the Church? and is it for this that you have gathered a multitude: that the possession of Christ may become your inheritance? or do you think that you will possess the silver and gold of the Church — which is understood of eloquence and meaning —, so as to take away its household goods and all its property, and seize the boundless booty gathered by Christ the victor?' 'Therefore, O prophet Ezekiel, who in the type of Christ are called son of man, speak to Gog and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: When, the error of the whole world having been taken away, my people Israel, which discerns God with the mind, dwells in the Church confidently or in peace, then you will know, or rise up and come from your place' — and what the place of heretical depravity is, the following word shows: From the sides of the north, which tries to chill all the warmth of the believers —. And many peoples will come with him, all riders of horses — of whom it is written: The horse and the rider he has cast into the sea —, a great company and a mighty army; with whom: 'You will go up', he says, 'against my people Israel like a cloud and darkness, to cover my land — of which it was spoken above —. In the last days you will be, in the time of the preaching of the Gospel, and I will bring you upon my land — For there must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest, and by the will of God the devil, the ἀνταγωνιστής [adversary], and all the dogmas of perversity have been left —, so that all the nations may know (and understand) me, when I am sanctified in you before their eyes, O Gog, that is, when through your punishments they have understood me as judge'. And he makes an apostrophe to Gog himself: 'Are you not he of whom I spoke in ancient days, by the hands of my servants the prophets of Israel?': that is, of Moses — who says in the book of Numbers, at least according to the Seventy: A man shall come forth from his seed and shall rule over very many nations, and Gog his kingdom shall be lifted up, and his kingdom shall increase, but according to the Hebrew I found it written thus: His king shall be taken away because of Agag, and his kingdom shall be removed, because the kingdom of Israel was destroyed in Saul on account of Agag king of Amalek; and in another place: He will cleanse the land of his people —; Joel too describes the peoples to be gathered in the valley of 'Iosaphat', that is, 'of the judgment of God'; and Isaiah, and all the prophets, in whose hands and good works the word of the Lord comes about. 'When therefore you come upon the land of Israel, my indignation will go up in my fury against you. And in my zeal for my people, in the fire of my wrath I have spoken, which is to consume all the timbers of your vices: At that', he says, 'time there will be a great commotion upon the land of Israel': for at the instigation of the devil frequent persecution will arise against the Church, and when it has been lulled to rest and overcome by the protection of God, then the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field, and every creeping thing that moves upon the earth, and all the men who are upon the face of the earth, will be moved before his face; which is clearly shown of the inhabitants of the Church, of whom some like the fish of the sea, some like the birds of the sky, some like the beasts of the field and all the creeping things that move upon the earth, others as retaining the dignity of man, dwell upon the face of the earth — and that diversity of conduct is signified by various names the Apostle also writes to the Corinthians, since he says that after the resurrection some bodies are heavenly, others earthly, one the body of a fish, another of a bird, another of beasts, another of creeping things, and another of men, who have kept their original name; in the Acts of the Apostles too, that sheet which is shown three times to the apostle Peter by its four corners signifies the variety of believers which was also contained in the ark of the flood —. Then, from the face of the Lord and from the sight of his majesty, the mountains which raised themselves against the knowledge of God will be overturned, and the hedges or valleys will fall, which either have sunk to the depths through lowness of understanding or at any rate promise some fortification so as to imitate the Church of God — of whose hedges it is said: Whoever breaks down a hedge, a serpent will bite him —, and every wall will collapse to the ground: for when the strength of the Church's word appears, all the fortifications of the heretics will collapse. 'And I will call together against him, that is, against Gog, the prince of the heretics, a sword on all my mountains, so that the princes of his army may be destroyed by the sword for the Lord'; then heresy will fight against heresy, and their fighting among themselves is our victory. And I will judge, he says, him with death (or pestilence) and blood and violent rain and immense stones (or of hail): and Gog is judged by his own death, and by the blood which he shed, and by violent rain, the words of a learned and perfect man, and by immense stones which overwhelm him with the testimonies of the Scriptures, or of hail, which make his heat grow cold — All, indeed, who commit adultery, their hearts are like an oven —. Fire, he says, and sulphur I will rain upon him, by which the punishment of eternal judgment is shown; and not only upon him who was the author of perversity, but also upon all his army and multitude and upon the many peoples who are with him — for the heretics have many companions, or rather the devil, their prince, is surrounded by an infinite multitude —. And when all error has been taken away and the princes of the heretics have been punished and destroyed, the Lord is magnified, and sanctified in the believers, and becomes known in the eyes of the many nations which have believed in his faith, and both from their own blessedness and from the punishments of the adversaries they will know and recognize that he himself is the Lord. These things we have interpreted as we were able, obeying that precept: You shall turn aside neither to the right nor to the left, but: You shall walk on the royal road; but if anyone finds fault with what is ours, let him either bring forward better things for us to follow, or, if he wishes to say nothing, let him leave perfect knowledge to God, provided only that he knows that it is by no means our powers, but our intention, that is to be judged.

39:1-16

But you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, prince of the head (or Ros) of Meshech and Tubal; and I will turn you about (or gather you) and lead you astray (or lead you down), and make you go up from the sides (or from the uttermost parts) of the north, and bring you upon the mountains of Israel. And I will strike (or destroy) your bow in your left hand (or from your left hand), and your arrows from your right hand, and I will cast you down upon the mountains of Israel. And you will fall, you and all your troops, and the peoples (or nations) that are with you; to the wild beasts, to the birds and to every winged thing and to the beasts of the earth I have given you to be devoured: on the face of the field (or plain) you will fall, for I have spoken, says the Lord God. And I will send fire on Magog, and on those who dwell in the islands confidently (or and the islands will be inhabited in peace), and they will know that I am the Lord. And I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will not pollute (or it will not be polluted) my holy name any more, and the nations will know that I am the Lord God, the holy one of Israel. Behold, it comes, and it has been done (or you will know that it will be), says the Lord; this is the day of which I have spoken. And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go forth, and will kindle and burn the weapons, the shield and the spears (or the targes and the pikes), the bow and the arrows, the hand staves and the pikes (or lances), and they will kindle them with fire seven years. And they will not carry (or will not take up) wood from the regions (or from the fields), nor cut it down from the forests, since they will kindle the weapons with fire; and they will plunder those whose prey they had been, and despoil their despoilers, says the Lord God. And it shall be, on that day, I will give Gog a renowned place, a sepulcher in Israel, the valley of the travelers east of the sea, which makes those who pass by stand aghast (or the πολυάνδριον [common burial ground, literally "place of many men"] of those who will come to the sea, and they will build round about the mouth of the valley); and there they will bury Gog and all his multitude, and it will be called the valley (or 'ge') of the multitude of Gog. And the house of Israel will bury them, to cleanse the land (or that the land may be cleansed) for seven months; and all the people of the land will bury them, and it will be for them a renowned day on which I was glorified, says the Lord God. And they will appoint men continually going through (or going round) the land, to bury and to search out those who remain upon the face of the land, that they may cleanse it; and after seven months they will begin to search, and they will go round traversing the land; and when they see a man's bone, they will set up a marker beside it, until the undertakers bury it in the valley (or 'ge') of the multitude of Gog. And the name of the city is Amona (or Πολυάνδριον), and they will cleanse the land (or the land will be cleansed). These things the heirs of the Jewish tradition and the disciples of endless fables contend will come to pass after the reign of a thousand years: that Gog, prince of Ros, Meshech and Tubal, is to be slain in the borders of Israel and to be devoured by all the winged creatures and the beasts; and that the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will for seven years by no means have the use of wood from the cutting of forests, but from the weapons of Gog, namely shields and spears and arrows and staves or pikes; and that Gog himself is to be buried in the valley which in Hebrew is called 'ge', and the name of his sepulcher is to be called πολυάνδριον, namely where a multitude of men has been buried; and that he is to be buried by the house of Israel for seven months so that the land may be cleansed, and that the day when Gog was slain will be renowned, and that men are to be appointed to search diligently for the bones and bury them, so that, namely, nothing remains unburied in the land; and that after the seven months, or within the seven months, the land is to be traversed, and wherever they observe a man's bone lying, it is to be pointed out by a marker set beside it, so that afterward those who have been put in charge of this work may bury it; and that the name of the city is to be called 'Amona', which in Greek is called Πολυάνδριον, that is, 'a multitude of buried men', and that in this way the land is to be cleansed. This is what they have said; but let us, holding to the sense of the explanation we have begun, discuss one by one the things we have set forth. Gog too has his own trinity, 'Ros' and 'Mosoch' and 'Thubal', that is, 'head' and 'madness' and 'all things', so that there is no vice that does not stand in Gog's possession. He will be led out, or turned about, and he will be stroked and coaxed so that, hoping for victory, he may be led to battle to be slain; and he will go up from the sides, or from the uttermost parts, of the north, from which evils blaze up over all the earth, and by that very one he will be brought upon the mountains of Israel, which we ought to understand as the apostles and apostolic men and men of the Church, so that, after he has been brought to the mountains of Israel, then the bow that is in his left hand may be struck, and the arrows that are held in the right hand: for he too imitates, in order to kill those whom he has deceived, the having of weapons on the left and on the right, through good report and bad — these are the arrows and these the darts of which the psalmist too speaks: For behold, sinners have bent the bow, they have made ready arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart, which fiery darts of the devil are to be quenched with the shield of faith —. And Gog, who had gone up upon the mountains of Israel, is cast down, or will fall, on those very mountains with all his army and all his troops; and he will be food for the wild beasts, the birds and every winged thing and the beasts of the earth, namely the adverse powers that ate the seed by the wayside, and the bloodthirsty beasts — for as it is written of the dragon: You gave him as food to the Ethiopian peoples, so all who are deceived by the heretics are the food of demons —: and Gog will fall either in the breadth of the plain or in that of the field which has been tilled by God's husbandmen; for it cannot be that the Lord's words should be void. Then fire will be sent on Magog, namely on those who received Gog's teaching, and on those who, like islands, are beaten by the waves of the world and think that they ought to be secure — that fire of which the Lord speaks: I came to send fire upon the earth, and how I will that it burn —: 'that all may know and understand that I am the Lord'. 'And let my holy name be made known in the midst of my people, which was by no means led astray by the authority of Gog, and let my name no longer be polluted among the heretics on the pretext of the knowledge falsely so called, and let the nations that are round about know that I am the Lord'. But what follows, Behold, it comes, and it has been done, is said of the judgment of Christ, who coming will come and will not delay; and this is the day of punishments and vengeance of which the Lord has spoken through all the prophets. And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go forth: the peoples of believers; and by the cities of Israel we understand the Church of right faith. And they will kindle and burn the weapons — of which it is written in another place too: He will crush the bow, he will shatter the weapons, and he will burn the shields with fire —, shields and spears, bow and arrows, hand staves — with which they celebrated a perverse Passover —, lances or pikes — with which they inflicted the broad and incurable wounds of their doctrines —, and shields, bows and arrows, of which it was said above. And what follows, And they will kindle them with fire seven years, is to be taken from Exodus and Leviticus, in which it is commanded by the law that in the seventh year, of release, when liberty is restored to Hebrew slaves and all debts are cancelled and the ancient possession returns to its owners, rest too is granted to the land and all the crops are given over to the poor; so that, namely, in seven years, a sacred and perfect number, the armor of the heretics may perish utterly, and the men of the Church may by no means cut wood from the fields and regions and woods and forests of the nations, whom they desire rather to save than to destroy, but from those of the heretics whom they have conquered, from shields, spears, arrows, staves and pikes and lances: for they too have various weapons for attacking the Church of Christ, which are to be set on fire by learned men with the fire of the Holy Spirit — namely by the Church's word, and whoever has it will be able to say: Was not our heart burning on the way, when Jesus opened the Scriptures to us? —; nor can we have full peace and confidence in our dwelling unless we plunder all the gear of our adversaries, so that everything may perish and be burned to ashes, and we plunder those who had earlier plundered us, and lay waste those who had first laid waste the Church. On that day — in the clear light of preaching — I will give, he says, Gog a renowned place, a sepulcher in Israel, according to the Hebrew: the valley of the travelers east of the sea, which makes those who pass by stand aghast; the sense of this saying is this: The sepulcher of Gog will not be on the mountains but in low valleys and rugged places — which in Hebrew are called 'ge'; and the heretics, though they are situated in the west, pretend that these are places of the east —, in order to deceive the travelers, namely those who pass through this world and are not inhabitants but sojourners — saying that prophetic word: I am a stranger and a sojourner, as all my fathers were —. For which of those passing by — of whom it is written: And those who passed by did not say: The blessing of the Lord be upon you! — does not marvel and stand aghast when he sees the valley of the travelers, which to the travelers seems a valley, to the inhabitants a mountain? This is according to the Hebrew. But the Seventy translated: the πολυάνδριον of those who will come to the sea, and they will build round about the entrance of the valley: for it is the labor of those who go out from the cities of Israel to shut and build round every entrance and exit of the heretical depravity, of those who had come to the sea and delighted in its bitterness, in the masses of its waves and in the cruelty of shipwreck, and to bury them in the chasms of the earth, so that they may no longer be able to go out and deceive anyone by their fraud. There, therefore, they will bury Gog and all his multitude, in which the heretics always delight; and the name of that valley in which Gog was buried will be called 'ge of the multitude', or πολυάνδριον, that is, 'the sepulcher of a very great multitude'. And as we said above that the weapons of the adversaries are kindled through seven years, so through seven months the land will be cleansed of the filth of the heretics; for from the first month — when we celebrate the Lord's Passover and escape the destroyer of Egypt by the blood of the lamb on our doorposts —, up to the end of the year — that is, up to the seventh month, when we pitch tabernacles and, among the other foliage, are sheltered also by branches of palms, so that a perfect victory over the enemies may be shown —, we fulfil all the festivals among the peoples; and not only the teachers but the whole people too will do this eagerly, to bury Gog, and cover him with earth, and by no means allow him to take in the free air. After the peace, however, and the slaying, or the burial, of Gog, men of the Church will be chosen who have this as their concern: that nothing of the former filth remain in the land of Israel, nothing of carrion; men to go through the land and search out the dead and bury them, so that, namely, the land of the Church may be cleansed. But if after seven months, when all things ought to have been purged, those who traverse and go round the land see that in anyone a man's bone — that is, the hardness of heretical depravity — or something of the carrion of the former doctrine has remained, they will set up, or build, a marker beside it, so that, after those who are of this kind have been marked, they may then either be corrected or be buried with Gog and thrust away into the throng of his burial. And the name of the city where the victory of the servants of the Lord is, and where the adversaries lie and the whole multitude of his enemies has been laid low, will be called 'Amona' or Πολυάνδριον, so that the end of all things may be the restoration of purity. Finally there follows: And they will cleanse the land, doubtless those of whom it is written above: They will begin to search, and will go round traversing the land.

39:17-29

Therefore you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Say to every bird and to all the fowl and to all the beasts of the field (or plain): Assemble and hasten, run together from every side (or round about) to my victim, which I have sacrificed for you, a great victim upon the mountains of Israel, that you may eat flesh and drink blood. You will eat the flesh of the mighty (or of giants), and you will drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs and of he-goats, and of fatted bulls and of all fat things; and you will eat fat to the full, and drink blood to drunkenness from the victim which I have sacrificed for you. And you will be filled at my table with horse and with mighty horseman (or giant), and with all men of war, says the Lord God. And I will set (or give) my glory among the nations (or among you), and all the nations will see my judgment which I have done, and my hand which I have laid (or brought) upon them; and the house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God from that day and thereafter, and all the nations will know that the house of Israel was taken captive for their iniquities, because they forsook me, and I hid (or turned away) my face from them, and delivered them into the hand of the foes (or of their enemies), and they all fell by the sword. According to their uncleannesses and their crimes (or iniquities) I dealt with them, and I hid (or turned away) my face from them. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Now I will bring back the captivity of Jacob, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will take up zeal for my holy name. And they will bear their confusion (or ignominy), and all the transgression by which they transgressed against me, when they dwell in their own land confidently (or in peace), fearing no one. And when I have brought them back from the peoples (or nations), and have gathered them from the lands of their enemies (or from the regions of the nations), and have been sanctified in them in the eyes (or in the sight) of very many nations, they will also know that I am the Lord their God, since I have carried them over into the nations (or since I have appeared to them among the nations), and have gathered them upon their own land, and have not left any of them there. And I will no longer hide (or turn away) my face from them, because I have poured out my spirit (or fury) upon the whole house of Israel, says the Lord God. (What we have translated according to the Hebrews: I will gather them upon their own land, and I will not leave any of them there, is not found in the Seventy; and again, where according to the Hebrews a blessing is set at the end: Because I have poured out my 'spirit', the Seventy translated 'fury', which pertains to anger, especially since in the Hebrew 'ruhi' is written, which properly means 'my spirit' and by no means 'my fury'.) But everything up to the place where the building of the temple follows, those we spoke of above, the Jews and our own Judaizers, refer to the last time: that the birds and the beasts are to be sated with the flesh of Gog and of all his army as with the fattest offerings, and that Israel is to be restored to its former state and by no means be assailed any longer by the nations, but that God will pour out his spirit upon them so that they may dwell in their own land: not all the nations, but properly the house of Israel. But we, following the tropology we have begun, say this: that the Lord calls together all the birds and all the beasts, to hand over to them the princes of the heretics to be devoured as the fattest offerings — and those to whom the adversaries are handed over are called birds and beasts either for their swiftness in running about into all things or for their savagery and cruelty: For the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved, and that they may learn not to blaspheme —; and they will eat a great and very fat victim: not elsewhere, but upon the mountains of Israel, which we ought to understand as the prophets and apostles and holy men — for upon them the teachers of contrary dogmas fall in ruin, and by them they perish wounded —, upon whom the Church is built, and, to speak more truly, upon the mountain of mountains — of which Isaiah speaks, and Micah: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce to us his way —. And these birds and these swift and cruel beasts will eat flesh and drink blood — which cannot possess the kingdom of God —. The flesh of the mighty, or of giants, who rebelled against the knowledge of God, and the blood of the princes, not of heaven but of the earth, who savored all earthly things, they will drink: the blood of rams, of lambs and of he-goats, or, according to the Seventy, of rams, of calves and of he-goats, so that it signifies three living creatures that are sacrificed among the victims of God: for the heretics too imitate the gentleness of the Church, but their oblation serves not for the worship of God but for the food of demons, and this is their fattest offering; and they are sated as if with fat, and they drink the blood of the deceived to drunkenness; but God sacrifices this victim through the men of the Church, so that the most wicked guests may be sated with the multitude of the deceived, and drink to vomiting and drunkenness. When you see holy men, learned in the divine Scriptures, cutting down the horses of the heretics and their riders — of which it is written: The horse and the rider he has cast into the sea —, and hewing down all the rebels and giants with their own blade, and shedding the blood of all the warriors of the knowledge falsely so called, then know that the table of the Lord has been prepared, that he may set his glory among all the nations that believe in his name. And the churches of the saints will understand his judgment which he has executed upon the adversaries, and the strong hand with which he struck them; and let the house of Israel know and recognize that he is the Lord their God — who said: I am the Lord your God — from the day of the Lord's victory for ever, and let them reflect that the house of Israel was once taken captive by the heretics and scattered through the whole world of perverse dogmas for this reason: that they forsook him who for a little while hid, or turned away, his face from them and delivered them into the hand of the heretics, and they fell, pierced through by their blade, because of their uncleannesses and iniquities; and this was the cause of his hiding and turning away his face from them. And having set forth the reasons — according to that which is written: There must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest — for the captivity of Israel, that is, of the Church, in which those dwell who see God, he now promises that he will bring back into the Church the captivity of Jacob, who had supplanted the Jewish people and afterward was himself supplanted by the frauds of the heretics; and that he will have mercy on the whole house of Israel, not according to the flesh but according to the spirit. And I will take up, he says, my zeal for my holy name, which was blasphemed among the nations because of the heretics, so that, after he has set them free, they may blush and be confounded because, having abandoned the faith of the Church, they transgressed against me. Let them be confounded, then, and blush very swiftly, when they dwell in their own land, the land of the meek and the land of the saints, and dwell confidently, or in peace, by no means fearing the snares of the heretics. Then they will be brought back from the peoples, and gathered from the lands of their enemies into their own land, and the Lord will be sanctified in them in the sight of very many nations, which themselves too are going to believe in the Lord; and let this be the end of blessedness: to know and recognize that he is the Lord their God, because he appeared to them among the nations, or carried them over from the nations, and gathered them upon their own land, the land of Judea, the land of confession, the land of the meek and the land of the living, and left not even one to heretical depravity. And let him no longer hide his face from them nor turn away from them, because he has poured out the spirit of his grace — of which the prophet Joel too speaks: In the last days I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh —; and he has poured it out upon the whole house of Israel. But if instead of 'spirit' we read 'fury' according to the Seventy, which is not found in the Hebrew, it is to be understood thus: that he no longer hides his face from those upon whom he had earlier poured out his fury. Thus far we have spoken on Ezekiel the prophet, with God, as we hope and believe, helping us and opening our mouth, not destroying the opinion of others, if any have written or will hereafter write, but offering our own, such as they are. But in the building of the temple, and the order of the priests, and the division of the holy land, and the river going out from the temple, and the trees on either bank, ever green and bearing fruit every month, and the rest that is contained in the prophetic volume up to its end, we openly confess our lack of skill, judging it better for the present to say nothing than to say too little.

Book Twelve

My trepidation in the explanation of the temple of Ezekiel, or rather my persistence in silence, is overcome by your prayers, daughter Eustochium, and by the promises of the Lord, who says: Ask and you will receive, seek and you will find, knock and it will be opened to you; and since we had made use of an excuse, so as to say at the end of the previous volume: 'It is better to say nothing than to say little', you turned it to the contrary, so that you think it preferable to say at least a little than nothing, because in the one there is a ready will, in the other despair of the whole work; and you remind me that the nature of men is of this kind, that they do not feel so much gratitude for what you have granted as resentment over what you have refused: for we praise virtues with less zeal than we censure vices, and, however beautiful bodies may be, they become the more conspicuous through the crookedness and deformity of a single member. I shall therefore comply with your wish, and I will spread my sails to the blowing Holy Spirit, not knowing to what shores I am to come, and crying out with this same prophet: From the four winds of heaven come, O spirit. And to the fastidious reader, or rather to a hostile mind that will read what is ours, I declare this with all frankness concerning the explanation of the temple: if he desires the truth, let him seek it from others; we, for our part, simply confess and dictate what we are able to conjecture in a most difficult work, ready to give thanks to the Lord if, not in all things — which is impossible — but in most, he has opened to us the doors of knowledge: For to one who pursues the first places, as the sublime orator says, it is honorable even to stop at the second or third.

40:1-4

In the twenty-fifth year of the exile (or of the captivity) of Jeconiah, at the beginning of the year (or in the first month), on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck (or taken), on this very day (or on that day), the hand of the Lord came upon me, and he brought me there, in visions (or in a vision) of God, and he brought me into the land of Israel, and set (or placed) me upon an exceedingly high mountain, upon which there was as it were the building of a city facing toward the south (or opposite). And he brought me in there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze (or of shining bronze), and a cord of linen (or of the masons) in his hand, and a measuring reed in his hand; and he was standing in the gate. And the same man spoke to me: Son of man, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you (or set in your heart all that I shall have shown you), for you have been brought (or have entered) here that they may be shown to you; and declare (or you shall show) all that you see to the house of Israel. If in the fifth year of the captivity or exile of King Jehoiachin, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, the heavens were opened to the prophet Ezekiel beside the river Chebar and he saw visions of God, but now it is said that in the twenty-fifth year of the exile of the same Jeconiah, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, the hand of the Lord came upon him, and he was brought into the land of Israel and placed upon an exceedingly high mountain, so that he might see the building of a city facing toward the south, no one doubts that his whole prophecy was woven together when nineteen years, and nine months and five days of the twentieth year, had been completed. But if, according to Theodotion, who in the place where we have put 'at the beginning of the year' translated 'in the new year', on the tenth day of the month — now among the Hebrews the new year is the name of the seventh month, which among them bears the name 'thesri' [Tishri], so that on the first day of the seventh month there is the blast of trumpets, and on the tenth day of the same month the day of fasting and propitiation, and on the fifteenth, when the whole orb of the moon is filled, the day of Tabernacles — it is given to be understood that the building of the city had been shown to Ezekiel on the tenth day, the day of the Lord's propitiation. And just as he showed the restoration of the people, or rather their bringing back to life, in the bones of the plain under the image of the resurrection, so now the Lord promises, under its description, the renewal of the city which fourteen years before had been destroyed by fire by the Babylonian, so that, as the type of the pot kindled from the face of the north had shown the captivity and the overthrow, and the truth of the prophecy had been proved by the event, so, from trust in things past, the truth of the building to come might be proved by the prophecy. Nor is this said of that time, as some unlearned among the Jews would have it, when under Zerubbabel and under Joshua son of Jehozadak, the great priest, the temple was built, while Haggai and Zechariah prophesied: for this temple which is now described, and the order of the priesthood, and the division and fertility of the land, is far more majestic than the one which Solomon had built; but the one which was built under Zerubbabel was so small and, in comparison with the former, of so little worth, that those who had seen the first temple and afterward looked upon this one wailed and bore witness to their grief with tears, and the cry of those lamenting was far greater than the blast of the trumpets; read the book of Ezra. Further, what is added: In the fourteenth year after the city was struck (or taken), according to the mystical senses signifies the fourteen generations from David to the nativity of Christ; when they were completed, the restoration of the city is promised by him of whom it is written: He himself will build my city and will bring back the captivity of my people, and again, he came: To proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, saying to those who were in chains: Come out, and to those who were in darkness: Be uncovered. Now the hand of the Lord comes upon him so that, though placed in Babylon according to the flesh, he might come in the spirit to the land of Israel, and might be set, not at all in a vision, but in the visions of God, upon an exceedingly high mountain — of which Isaiah and Micah prophesy: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob —, which mountain is exceedingly high in comparison with the other mountains — of which the prophet testifies, saying: I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where my help shall come, and in another place: Mountains are round about it, and the Lord is round about his people, of which it is also said in Isaiah: Go up onto a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion —; upon this mountain is shown the building of a city, according to the Seventy and Aquila 'opposite' and 'over against the north', from where the prophet had come to the land of Israel, but according to Theodotion and Symmachus 'facing toward the south', where the light is full and the sun of righteousness is set at the highest summit of heaven — whence it is also said in the Song of Songs: Arise, north wind, and come, south wind; blow through my garden, and let its spices flow; for the north wind, the harshest of winds, is driven away from the Lord's garden, so that the warmth of love may not grow cold and the flowers may not wither —; and when it is said: As it were the building of a city, not truly a city but the likeness of a city is shown — of which it is written: Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God, which is: Jerusalem, built as a city, whose sharing of it is in the selfsame, and in which: Great is the Lord and exceedingly to be praised, in the city of our God, on his holy mountain, and: In the towers of the city God is known to the righteous, when he upholds it, of which it is said elsewhere too: The rush of the river makes glad the city of God, and: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden, which speaks in Isaiah: I am a strong city, a city which is besieged — he did not say: which 'is stormed', but 'is besieged' —, which 'is built upon the rock and is shaken by no storm' —. There follows: 'And he brought me in there — the hand of the Lord is understood; and 'there', that is, 'as it were the building of a city' —, so that he might show me all the things that were within'. Behold, he says, a man whose appearance (or vision) was like the appearance of gleaming bronze — he, namely, of whom it is written: Behold a man, the Orient is his name —; now he had an appearance by no means of electrum, as is said at the beginning of this volume, nor was he girded with a golden belt, as is contained in the Revelation of John, but he had an appearance, according to the Hebrew, as of bronze — for this material is more resonant than all the metals and rings out far with its clang; hence also in Daniel, in the image which was put together from gold, silver, bronze and iron, the kingdom of Alexander and of the Greeks is shown in the likeness of bronze, so that the eloquence of the Greek language might be signified; by which it is plain that those who do not yet know the full mysteries of the temple that is to be built spiritually are still in need of teaching —; there was also a cord of linen, or of the masons, in his hand — of which it is also written in Zechariah that he had a surveyor's cord, to measure the breadth and the length of the city. And of the masons: either of the angels who ministered at God's command, or of Moses and of all the prophets and apostles who build the city of God and are helpers or ministers of the Lord's will; hence the apostle Paul also said: We are God's husbandry, God's building —. And what follows: And a measuring reed in his hand, designates the prophetic grace — of which it is written in Psalm 44 (45): My tongue is the reed of a scribe writing swiftly, and of John, prophet and baptist: What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed shaken by the wind?, which reed those desire to imitate who writing, write iniquity, and upon whom the prophet calls down a curse, saying: Rebuke the beasts of the reed —. And he was standing in the gate, because through him we go in to the Father, and without him we cannot enter the city of God, so that he may receive the worthy and cast out the unworthy; in the gate too there is judgment — whence the prophet also says: They hated those who reprove in the gate, and in another place: They shall not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies in the gate —. This man spoke to the prophet, he in whose hand was the cord, and whose appearance was as of bronze, and who held the reed in his hand: the true architect spoke to Ezekiel — he whom the apostle Paul imitated, saying: As a wise architect I have laid the foundation; and he calls the architect wise to distinguish him from the one who is foolish and in Zechariah is called the foolish shepherd —; and he spoke the words that follow: Son of man, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears, not with the eyes of the flesh but of the spirit, nor with the ears of the body but of the soul —. Lift up, he says, your eyes and see, for the harvests are already white for reaping, and: He who has ears to hear, let him hear —; and the building of the city is seen, and the order of the ceremonies and of the priests and the description of the land are heard; nor was it enough to have commanded him to see with his eyes and hear with his ears, but he added: And set your heart upon all (or and set in your heart all) that I shall show you; for it profits nothing to have seen and to have heard, unless you have laid up in the treasury of memory the things you have seen and heard; and when he says: All that I shall show you, he makes him an attentive hearer, makes him ready too with the eyes of the heart, so that he may hold in memory the things that are to be shown to him: For you have been brought here that all things may be shown to you — by which saying he shows in a special way that nothing is sweeter than contemplation and knowledge, which the prophet desires, saying: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, that I may see the will of the Lord and visit his temple; whence he adds and says: Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house, and the place of the dwelling of your glory —. 'Declare', he says, 'all that you see to the house of Israel, so that those who cannot see by themselves may learn through you the things that are shown to you by the Lord'; and to the house of Israel: to those who behold God with the mind — among whom was Nathanael too, who sought Christ most zealously and was found worthy to hear: Behold a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile —.

40:5-13

And behold, a wall outside, round about the house on every side, and in the man's hand a measuring reed of six cubits and a handbreadth; and he measured the breadth of the building, one reed, the height also, one reed. And he came to the gate which looked toward the eastern way, and he went up by its steps, and he measured the threshold of the gate, one reed in breadth, that is, one threshold one reed in breadth, and the cell one reed in length and one reed in breadth, and between the cells five cubits, and the threshold of the gate beside the vestibule of the gate within, one reed. And he measured the vestibule of the gate, of eight cubits, and its front, two cubits; and the vestibule of the gate was within. Further, the cells of the gate toward the eastern way, three on this side and three on that, one measure of the three, and one measure of the fronts on either side. And he measured the breadth of the threshold of the gate, ten cubits, and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits, and the margin before the cells, of one cubit, and one cubit the boundary on both sides; and the cells were of six cubits on this side and on that. And he measured the gate from the roof of a cell to its roof, a breadth of twenty-five cubits, door opposite door. (LXX: "And behold, a wall outside the house round about, and in the man's hand a measuring reed of six cubits and a palaestes; he measured the wall, the breadth equal to the reed, and the height of the same measure. And he went into the gate which looked toward the east, by seven steps, and he measured ÷ the 'thee', six on this side and six on that: the aelam of the gate equal to the reed in length and equal to the reed in breadth, and the 'aelam' in the middle of the 'theelatha', of five cubits, and the second 'thee' equal to the reed in breadth and equal to the reed in length, and the 'aelam' of five cubits, and the third 'thee' equal to the reed in breadth and equal to the reed in length, of the three, and the 'aelam' of the gate which is beside the 'aelam' of the gate, of eight cubits, and the 'aeleu' of two cubits, and the 'aelam' of the gate within. And the 'thee' of the gate opposite, three on this side and three on that, and one measure of the three, one measure of the 'aelam' on this side and on that. And he measured the breadth of the entrance of the gate, ten cubits, and the breadth of the gate, thirteen cubits, and one cubit was drawn in before the 'theeri', of one cubit, and a boundary of one cubit on this side and on that; and the 'thee' of six cubits on this side and of six cubits on that. And he measured the gate from the wall of the 'thee' to the wall of the 'thee', a breadth of twenty-five cubits; this gate opposite gate.") When I was a boy at Rome and was being educated in liberal studies, I used, with others of the same age and purpose, to go round the tombs of the apostles and martyrs on the Lord's days, and often to enter the crypts which, dug out in the depths of the earth, have along the walls, on either side of those who enter, the bodies of the buried; and everything is so dark that that prophetic word is almost fulfilled: Let them go down alive into hell, and light let in rarely from above tempers the horror of the darkness, so that you would think it not so much a window as a hole for the light let down; and again one moves forward step by step and, to those surrounded by blind night, that line of Vergil presents itself: Horror everywhere for the mind, and at the same time the very silences terrify. Let this have been said by me so that the prudent reader may understand what view I hold about the explanation of the temple of the Lord in Ezekiel, of which it is written: Cloud and darkness under his feet, and again: Darkness is his hiding place; whence Moses too entered into the cloud and the darkness, so that he could contemplate the mysteries of the Lord, which the people, placed far off and remaining below, could not see; and then, after forty days, the ignoble crowd with darkened eyes could not look upon the face of Moses, because the face of Moses 'had been glorified', or, as is contained in the Hebrew, 'was horned'; so it happens to me too as I read the description of the mystical temple — which the Jews think is to be built according to the letter at the coming of their Christ, whom we prove to be Antichrist, and which we refer to the Church of Christ, and which I see being built daily in the saints —: for wherever the eye of the heart is opened, and I have thought that I see something and hold the bridegroom — and rejoicing have said: I have found him whom my soul sought; I will hold him and will not let him go —, again the divine word deserts me, and the bridegroom flees from my hands, and my eyes are closed in blindness — so that I am compelled to say: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!, and what is written elsewhere: The judgments of the Lord are a great deep, and: Out of the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my voice, and that word of Elisha, who followed with the eyes of the heart the master snatched away from him, saying: Father, father, the chariot of Israel and its charioteer —. It must therefore be simply confessed that I do not wish to discuss the temple of blessed Ezekiel, about which all the ages have been silent, out of rashness, but desire, in faith and the fear of God, to show readers the conjecture of my mind, so that, if I offer to the tabernacle of God goats' skins and hair, by which the thorns and stings of sins may be covered and the rains of storms kept off, another, who is rich, may offer, according to the quality of his merits, either iron or bronze or silver and gold and most precious stones, and may not despise our gifts because they are lesser, but rejoice in his own wealth: for unless there are lowest things, there cannot be highest ones, and so that the greater may be praised, they grow by comparison with the lesser. Let us see, then, what Ezekiel, having entered the building of the city facing toward the south, first saw, then heard: And behold, he says, a wall outside, round about the house on every side. In place of the 'wall' which Aquila and Theodotion translated, Symmachus and the Seventy put περίβολος [enclosure]: on every side it surrounded the house, that is, the temple of the Lord; and the man whose appearance was as of bronze had not only the surveyor's cord, the cord of the masons, but he also held in his hand the reed, whose measure was passed over in silence above and is now given: of six cubits and a handbreadth — which in Greek is more correctly called palaestes, and is the sixth part of a cubit; otherwise 'palmus' means σπιθαμὴν [a span], which some have been accustomed to call 'palma' [palm] for the sake of distinction, and further to call the 'palaesten' 'palmum' [handbreadth] —; with this reed, then, he measured the breadth and the height of the wall, and both, that is, height and breadth, were of one reed, that is, of six cubits and one handbreadth. Though there were very many gates, he would not enter by the other gates, but by the one which looked toward the eastern quarter; and because the place was not level — for the wall round about, and the house of God itself, had been built on higher ground —, he therefore goes in, or rather climbs up, by steps — which the Seventy alone name as 'seven', whereas both in the Hebrew and in the other translators we read only 'steps', without a number —; and having entered the gate, he at once measured the threshold of the gate — which the Seventy name 'thee', in place of which in the Hebrew is written 'seph' [threshold]; and I think the diligent and studious reader should be reminded of this, if indeed he is led by knowledge of the Scriptures and not by the empty declamations of orators: that he should know that almost all the Hebrew words and names which have been set down in the Greek and Latin translation have been corrupted by excessive age and depraved by the fault of the scribes, and that, as ever more uncorrected copies are written from uncorrected ones, out of Hebrew words Sarmatian words have been made, or rather words of no nation, since they have ceased to be Hebrew and have not begun to be foreign —. The threshold of the gate, then — or 'thee', or rather 'seph', which Symmachus translated οὐδὸν [threshold], Aquila and Theodotion πρόθυρον [front doorway] —, had one reed, that is, six cubits and a handbreadth, in breadth; further, meaning I know not what, the Seventy added of their own 'six on this side and six on that'; and after the threshold of the gate, according to the Hebrew, he measured the cell — or room, and, as Symmachus translated, παραστάδας, that is, 'posts' — on either side, at one reed, as much in length as in breadth — which the Seventy also translated 'aelam', and which in what follows Symmachus translated 'fore-threshold' —; and between the two cells — or rooms and παραστάδας — there were five cubits, and another near-threshold of the gate beside the vestibule within, of one reed; a third, the vestibule of the gate, also had eight cubits, and in its front, or in its margins, two cubits; and lest anyone think this vestibule to be the same as the one above, he added: the vestibule of the inner gate; in place of which the Seventy translated a first and a second and a third vestibule. And the cells, that is, the rooms which had been built in the vestibules after the eastern gate, looked toward the eastern way; and so that we may know how many cells there were, it is added: three on this side and three on that, looking, namely, toward the north and toward the south and toward the eastern way; and there was one measure of the fronts on either side. He also measured the measure of the threshold of the gate in breadth and found ten cubits, and in length thirteen cubits, and the ends of the cells — or, as Symmachus translated, παραστάδες — were narrowed into one cubit, and each front had one cubit; and the cells, or παραστάδες and, as the Seventy put of their own, 'theelatha' —, had six cubits each on either side. And he measured the gate from the roof of a cell — or παραστάδος — to its roof or wall, and found, between roof and roof, twenty-five cubits of breadth, for so much was the space between door and door, or between gate and gate. Let us have said these things briefly, in the spirit of one divining rather than explaining, wishing to sketch, according to the letter, a picture that is obscure and almost invisible; for the rest, we shall set down, briefly and with hesitation, the few things we can conjecture. The apostle Paul, wishing the Ephesians to know the more sacred things, prays for them 'that they may be filled with the wisdom and love of the Lord, and, being rooted, may be able to know and comprehend what is the breadth and length and height and depth of his riches'; and to the same he says: So then you are by no means strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens of the saints and members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the cornerstone; in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy temple for the Lord, in whom you too are built up into a dwelling place of God in the Holy Spirit. Peter too, in almost the same words, because with the same spirit, says in his epistle: If indeed you have believed that the Lord is good. Coming to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen and honored by God, you yourselves too, as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house, into a holy priesthood, offering spiritual victims acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. From this it is clear that the Lord Savior, who is the true architect, tests the stones: which can be called together into the foundation of the temple, which into the middle, which into the higher places, and which, being of lesser measure or of not so solid firmness, into the wall and outside the temple, into the περιβολῇ round about — for it is a thing of no small strength nor of the least firmness to bear the stones laid on from above; whence the apostle writes to believers: Bearing one another's burdens, and in another place it is written that we ought not to take up a weight which we cannot carry —. And the measuring reed, which had six cubits and one handbreadth, signifies this: that our way of life is known to God, which is contained in the six days in which the world was made, and that the reason of each of our works is known too, so that one thing pertains to works, another to the mind; whence also the breadth is equal to the height, and of these the breadth refers, as we have said, to works, the height to the mind, which hastens toward high things. Let it suffice to have given this warning once: that I know that cubitum and cubita [cubit, cubits] are used in the neuter gender, but that, for simplicity of understanding and by the custom of the common people, I also put them in the masculine gender — for it is not our concern to avoid faults of speech, but to explain the obscurity of holy Scripture in whatever words we can —. The man, then, whose name is Orient, goes in by the eastern gate, to enlighten those whom he found at the first front of the vestibule, or at the very entrance of the gate: not by one step but by several, whose number is passed over in silence so that the difficulty of the ascent may appear, and so that, however many steps you propose to yourself, you may know that it is less than what is left in doubt — I think this is the gate of which it is also sung in the Psalms: This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter by it —; and he measured the threshold of the gate, so that we may be able to know that all things lie open to the knowledge of God; this threshold is said to be of one reed in breadth, and nothing is said of its height and length: for it is a way and an entrance, and through it one must proceed to the inner parts — although in this place the Seventy superfluously said 'length' or, as is contained in most manuscripts, 'height' —; and the rooms, that is, the cells and παραστάδες, have one reed each, as much in length as in breadth, but between cell and cell there are only six cubits, so that the inner parts of the rooms may have the full measure of the reed, that is, of six cubits and a handbreadth, while works and reason agree alike, but those things which are outside, that is, between cell and cell, five cubits; for they have not yet penetrated the secrets of Christ, nor can they say: The king has brought me into his room, and elsewhere: All the glory of the king's daughter is within, but, while the disciples stay at home with Christ, they cannot hear his mysteries, and they desire the word of God to come out to them outside; and therefore the measure of five cubits is set in them, so that they may be taught to refer all things to the five senses; the threshold of the other gate too, or, as is contained in the Seventy, of the second and the third vestibule, is of the same measure of one reed. After this, for its vestibule, that is, for the threshold of the gate, the entrance, eight cubits are set, so that the inner parts of the vestibule may hold not the number seven, and six cubits and one handbreadth, but the number eight, which pertain to the mystery of the resurrection and of the Lord's day. 'And on the front', he says, 'of the same vestibule there were two cubits', which pertain either to both Testaments, or to the letter and the spirit, or to the mystery of the tongs with which, in Isaiah, the coal is taken from the altar and carried to cleanse the prophet's lips; and so that we may know what this vestibule is which is bounded by eight and two cubits, he puts it more plainly: And the vestibule of the gate was within, through which we come to the temple of God. The cells too, and rooms, which were toward the way of the eastern gate, in place of which the Seventy write 'aeleu', were three on this side and three on that, of one measure, that is, of one reed which had six cubits and one handbreadth, of which it was spoken above, and the 'aelam' one reed in length and one reed in breadth, and between the cells five cubits; so, lest we should think that there were only two cells, he set three on either side, to show the number six, which is shown also in the water jars of the Gospel, in which the waters were changed into wines; and daily the Jewish waters are turned into wine, which makes glad the heart of man, and becomes sweeter with the blood of Christ.
