and he who flees fornication and renders to his wife her due, coming together again lest Satan tempt him, will hear with the people of Israel: On this day I have taken away from you the reproach of Egypt; he will also use clothes that keep off the cold, not those that by their thinness show bodies naked —: the flesh worn down by fasts and circumcised by continence escapes the reproach of the Egyptians: Who are of great flesh — and it can say that which is read in most copies according to the edition of the Seventy: As my flesh has wasted away, in a land desert and pathless and waterless, so in the holy place I have appeared to you —. If ever, then, we wish to bring foreigners into the temple of God, let us circumcise their ears and lips and heart and all their flesh, and their eyes, taste and smell: so that we may do all things with the fear of God and with reason; let the bishops and presbyters and the whole ecclesiastical order hear this, that they may not bring in alien sons uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, lest they be in his sanctuary and pollute his house; for if they do this, what follows will be fitted to them: And you offer my loaves — the loaves, namely, of proposition, in all the churches and throughout the world, springing up from the one bread —, and not only the loaves but also the fat — of which it is written: He fed them with the fat of the wheat —, and the blood — which was poured out in the passion of Christ —. And it must be read thus, and the order of the reading rendered so: 'Since you bring alien sons, uncircumcised in heart and in body, into my sanctuary and pollute my house, you dare to offer loaves and fat and blood — the mystic sacraments — and you do not understand what you have dissolved, and that you have transgressed my covenant in all your crimes and impieties; and that you have not kept the precepts of my sanctuary nor set keepers of my ceremonies in my sanctuary' — and the whole threat is against those who have not heeded the Apostle warning beforehand: Lay hands hastily on no one, and do not share in other men's sins —; or certainly it must be understood thus: 'You have dissolved my covenant in all your crimes and have not kept the precepts of my sanctuary, and you dare to set unworthy and alien keepers in the observance of my sanctuary — so that 'for yourselves' is understood, not 'for me', and the sense is —: who serve you and minister to you in carnal things, and for the sake of your comforts pollute my sanctuary'.

44:9-16

Thus says the Lord God: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my sanctuary, no alien son who is in the midst of the sons of Israel. But also the Levites who went far away from me in the straying of the sons of Israel, and strayed from me after their idols, shall bear their iniquity, who were in my sanctuary temple-keepers and doorkeepers of the gates of the house and ministers of the house: and they slaughtered the holocausts and the victims of the people, and they stood before them to minister to them. Because, then, they ministered to them in the sight of their idols and became to the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they have borne their iniquity. And they shall not draw near to me to exercise the priesthood for me, nor shall they approach any of my sanctuary next to the Holy of Holies, but they shall bear their shame and their crimes which they committed. And I will make them doorkeepers of the house in all its service and in all that is done in it. But the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the ceremonies of my sanctuary when the sons of Israel strayed from me, they shall approach me to minister to me, and they shall stand in my sight to offer me the fat and the blood, says the Lord God. They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table, to minister to me and to keep my ceremonies. (LXX: "Therefore thus says the Lord: No foreign son uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my holy places, among all the sons of foreigners who are in the midst of the house of Israel. But also the Levites who went away from me when Israel strayed from me after their own thoughts, and they shall receive their iniquities, and they shall be in my holy places ministering, porters at the gates of the house and ministers of the house: they shall sacrifice the holocausts and the victims for the people, and they shall stand before the people to minister to them, because they ministered to them before the face of their idols, and it became to the house of Israel a torment of iniquity. Therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they shall receive their iniquity: that they may not approach me to exercise the priesthood for me, nor to offer at all the holy things of the sons of Israel nor at my Holy of Holies, and they shall bear their disgrace in the error in which they strayed. And they shall appoint them to keep the charges of the house in all its works and in all that they have done in it. The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charges of my holy places when the house of Israel strayed from me, they shall approach me to minister to me, and they shall stand before my face to offer me the sacrifice, the fat and the blood, says the Lord God. They shall enter into my holy places, and they shall approach my table, to minister to me and to observe my charges.") I have set down the testimony according to both editions, so that by comparing them we may be able to know what the Seventy meant and what the Hebrew contains. The Seventy signify this: that foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh, who dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel, ought not to enter the sanctuary of God; but that the Levites, that is, the priestly rank, who went far away from the Lord in the straying of the sons of Israel and strayed after their idols, after they have received their iniquity, are to stand in the sanctuary of the Lord as temple-keepers and doorkeepers and ministers of the house, and slaughter the holocausts and victims of the people, and be in their sight to minister to them, because they ministered to them in the sight of their idols and became to the house of Israel a torment of iniquity; and that the Lord God therefore says he has lifted up his hand against them, so that they may not approach him and exercise the priesthood for him nor offer for him in the Holy of Holies, and may bear their disgrace in the error in which they strayed: so that, namely, they are appointed to the observance of the charges of the house in all its works and in all that is done in the house — but if this is so, how can it stand that the Levites — who went far away from God in the straying of the sons of Israel and strayed from him after their idols — should themselves minister in the house and slaughter the holocausts and victims of the people, and themselves stand in their sight to minister to them — for what more are the priests, the sons of Zadok, to do, who kept the ceremonies of the sanctuary of God, of whom he says: They shall approach me to minister to me, and they shall stand in my sight to offer me the fat, and the rest —? —. But the Hebrew has this sense: 'No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh shall enter my sanctuary, even though he seems to be with the people of Israel. But the Levites, that is, the priestly rank, who went far away from me in the straying of the sons of Israel and followed idols, shall bear their iniquity, because they were in my sanctuary ministering in the office of the gates of the house and its ministers: for they offered the holocaust and the victims of the people, and they stood in their sight to minister for them. Because, then, they ministered for them in the sight of their idols and were to the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they have borne their iniquity. And they shall not draw near to me to exercise the priesthood for me, nor shall they approach any of my sanctuary next to the Holy of Holies, but they shall bear their shame and their crimes which they committed — for instead of the priestly office, they who had been accustomed to offer the holocaust and the victims and every sacrifice will be reduced to the lowest rank —. And they will be doorkeepers of the house, to everlasting disgrace — so that they may be seen by the whole people, entering and going out, from what lofty dignity they have come to what lowest rank —. But the priests,' he says, 'that is, the Levites who are the sons of Zadok — that is, of the righteous, or of the righteous one of God — and who in the time of the straying of all Israel kept the ceremonies of my sanctuary, they shall approach me to minister to me, and shall stand in my sight and offer me the fat — that is, the richest sacrifice —, and the blood — that is, a living sacrifice and pleasing to God —. And they shall enter my sanctuary and approach my table, to burn incense to me and to keep the whole rite of sacrifice' — but if this is so, that those who in the time of error or of persecution followed idols which they had fashioned from their own heart, and asserted not only by voice but also by the subscription of their hand that the Son of God is a creature: And they served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever: how do they assume for themselves the priestly and pontifical eminence, and dare to offer victims to God, they who were once worshipers of idols? — but, as the most ardent poet testifies: Whatever is sinned by many goes unpunished; the multitude of sinners has made pardon easier for the impious to obtain: so that those who, reduced to the laity, ought to have bewailed the former crimes of their sacrilege, now sit leaning back on the pontifical throne, and belch at us the nauseas of a feigned faith, nay rather the open epitomes of a misborn perfidy —; let them hear, then, at least late, and observe the precepts of almighty God: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh shall enter my sanctuary, though he be a son, though joined by kinship, though he cling to us by an old bond: if he is uncircumcised in heart or flesh, let him not be brought into the sanctuary of God, lest we make the ministers of Christ our own ministers, and pollute the altars of the Lord for the sake of carnal comforts —. Where we have put: And I will make them doorkeepers of the house in all its service and in all that is done in it, them, namely, of the Levites who went far away from God in the straying of the sons of Israel and followed idols to which they sacrificed victims, Symmachus, considering the order of the reading and its sense, translated more correctly, saying: For I had made them keepers of the doors of the house, of all its service and of all that is done in it, so that it does not refer to those who are to be in the temple, but to those who were.

44:17-21

And when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with garments (or robes) of linen, and nothing woollen shall come upon them (or and they shall not be clothed with woollens) while they minister in the gates (or from the gates) of the inner court and within. Linen fillets shall be on their heads (or they shall have linen turbans upon their heads), and linen breeches shall be on their loins, and they shall not be girded in sweat (or violently). And when they go out to the outer court to the people, they shall put off their garments (or robes) in which they had ministered, and they shall lay them (or them) up in the chambers (or exedras) of the sanctuary (or of the holy places), and they shall clothe themselves in other garments (or robes), and they shall not sanctify the people in their garments (or robes). But they shall not shave their head, nor let their hair grow long, but clipping they shall clip their heads (or: They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not crop their hair close; covering they shall cover their heads). And no priest shall drink wine when he has entered into the inner court. First the words of the history must be laid open. Among the other things which the word of the Lord commanded the priests, it orders this too to be observed: that in the very gates of the inner court they be clothed with garments — that is, robes — of linen, and that they not use woollen clothing, whether in the gates of the inner court or within — that is, in the inner shrines and the Holy of Holies —; that linen fillets too — or turbans — be on their heads, linen breeches on their loins; and what follows according to the Seventy: And they shall not be girded violently (for which Aquila and Symmachus translated in sweat, Theodotion expressing the Hebrew word itself, 'in ieze', Aquila's second edition 'buza'), by which he signifies that they are not to be girded violently, tightly and constrictedly like men in bonds, lest in the priestly and Levitical ministries they become unfit both to hold and to slay the victims, and be unable also to drag them and to run about. And because he had once commanded what garments the priests ought to use when they are within at their ministries, he orders again that, going out into the chambers — or exedras — of the holy places, they put off their former garments and put on others, lest, if they have the holy garments, they sanctify the people placed outside, who have not yet been sanctified nor prepared themselves for the sanctification of the temple, so as to be a Nazirite of the Lord; by which we learn that we ought not to enter the Holy of Holies in everyday garments, any whatever, polluted by the use of common life, but to hold the sacraments of the Lord with a clean conscience and clean garments. As for what follows: But they shall not shave their head, nor let their hair grow long, but clipping they shall clip their heads, it is clearly shown that we ought neither to have shaven heads like the priests and worshipers of Isis and Serapis, nor again to let our hair hang down, which is properly the mark of the luxurious and of barbarians and soldiers, but that the seemly bearing of priests should be shown at first sight; as for what the Seventy said: They shall not shave their heads, and they shall not crop their hair close, but covering they shall cover their heads, according to them we learn that baldness is not to be made with the razor, nor is the head to be cropped so close that it seems like those of the shaven, but the hair is to be let grow only so far that the skin is covered — or certainly that the priests are always to cover their heads, according to that line of Vergil: Covered, to veil his locks with a purple mantle; but this is a forced interpretation —. And wine the priests and Levites shall not drink, not only for their ministry, but indeed when they are about to enter the Holy of Holies, lest the mind be weighed down and the understanding become duller — hence the Apostle too says: It is good, he says, not to drink wine and not to eat meat, and in another place: And wine, in which is debauchery — for The people ate and drank, and rose up to play —; and what he grants Timothy, to drink a little wine, he clearly shows why he granted it: For your stomach, he says, and your frequent infirmities —. The priests of Egypt use linen garments not only within but without — but the divine religion has one dress for the ministry, another for common use —; and the fillets and breeches are rightly put on, so that seemliness and decorum may be preserved — namely, lest in climbing the steps of the altar and running about at the ministries they uncover their shame —; shaven heads belong to the superstition of the Gentiles; but from wine, as far as my knowledge goes, I do not think any of the Gentiles abstains. What all these things indicate according to the spiritual sense, what follows will show. That there are holy and spiritual garments the Apostle teaches, saying: Put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and in another place: Put on the bowels of mercy, goodness, humility, meekness and patience, and again: Strip off the old man with his works, and put on the new, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of the Creator; and I think this too signifies the same: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. And when this corruptible has put on incorruption — and this mortal immortality —, then shall come to pass the word that is written, and the rest — concerning the priestly garments it is written more fully in Exodus, and we once published a book to whose interpretation the diligent reader must be sent: for we cannot comprehend a broad subject in a brief discourse —; these garments we make for ourselves by our own labor, woven from the top — such as the tunic which the Lord also had, which cannot be torn —, and we are clothed with them when we know the secrets and hidden things of the Lord and have the spirit which searches even the high and deep things, which are not to be shown to the crowd nor brought out to the people who are not sanctified nor prepared for the holiness of the Lord — lest, if they hear things greater than themselves, they be unable to bear the majesty of knowledge and be choked, as it were, by solid food, they who are still to be nourished with the milk of infancy —; but that there are, on the contrary, very evil garments the divine Scripture teaches, as is that which is sung in the Psalms of Judas the traitor: And he put on cursing like a garment, and a little after: Let it be to him like a garment which is wrapped about him, and like a girdle with which he is always girded: hence the Lord too, who suffered for us and bore our sins, is said in Zechariah to have filthy garments — of which it is written: And Jesus was clothed in filthy garments —, which he afterward lays aside — as Scripture says: Take the filthy garments from him and clothe him with a full-length robe, and the rest —. As for what follows: Linen fillets (or turbans) shall be on their heads, I think it shows the crown of grace of which it is written: For your head shall receive a crown of graces; nor let that which the Apostle says about the uncovered and bared head raise a question for us: A woman ought to have authority over her head because of the angels. For if a woman is not veiled, let her be shorn; but if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered. For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of the man: for if it belongs to men not to cover the head, it seems contradictory how the priests are now ordered to cover their heads with linen fillets or a turban; but let us read more carefully: the present words will be resolved from the preceding ones: for it is said above: When all minister in the gates of the inner court and within — for if we enter into the holy places and stand in the sight of the Lord, we ought to cover our heads, because: No living man shall be justified in the sight of the Lord, and from infancy the heart of man is set on malice —; and further, we use breeches within, lest any shame of a polluted conscience and of the marriage act appear in the sight of the Lord: with which breeches the Savior also girds his apostles, saying: Let your loins be girded, and lamps burning in your hands, and the Apostle says to believers: Stand therefore, having your loins girded in truth, and let the imitators of Christ hear what is written of him: He shall be girded with righteousness about the loins and encompassed with truth; and with this very holy Levitical girdle he who is holy and has climbed to the summit of the virtues is by no means bound violently, lest he seem to keep the good of continence unwillingly and to eat bread in the sweat of his face, rather than to do the Lord's precept with his will. Further, when he goes outside and mingles with the people, he lays aside the priestly garments in the chamber in which the riches of the Lord are kept, and the priests use other garments and other teaching for the common crowd, lest the people be sanctified in their robes: for it is a grave thing to take up the burden of the multitude beyond one's strength, as Solomon says: It is a snare to a man to sanctify hastily anything of his own: for when he has made a vow, repentance steals upon him. — Further, the Nazirites too offer themselves of their own accord; and whoever has vowed anything and has not fulfilled it is guilty of the vow; hence it is also said of widows: When they have grown wanton in Christ, they wish to marry, having condemnation because they have made void their first faith — for It is better not to promise than to promise and not to perform —: Hannah offered Samuel, who remained in perpetual holiness; and Manoah offered his son Samson, but the lust of Delilah defiled the consecration of his hair: then the Lord departed from him and he was condemned to blindness, except that afterward, as his hair grew, he received his former strength, and, in a type of Christ, by far more of the foreigners did he kill in death than in life —. And the Lord wills his priests to have perpetual hair of consecration and to cover their heads, not with any veil from outside but with their own natural hair, not for ornament and luxury but for seemliness — hence the hairs of the head of the apostles too are numbered, as the Savior says: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered: of that head of which it is also written in Ecclesiastes: The eyes of the wise man are in his head. And the head of the man is Christ, which the sinner tramples and despises and, so to speak, shaves with a razor and takes away its beauty: which the Ammonites also did to those whom David had sent as envoys —; but if transgression of the law dishonors God, it follows that he who keeps the precepts of the law honors him — that what is written may be fulfilled: That all may honor the Son, as they honor the Father —. Further, as for what follows, that: No priest, when he is about to enter the inner court, shall drink wine, it is clear that by drunkenness and strong drink the state of the mind is overturned, and that we are not fully wise when the mind is taken up with wine and satiety; but drunkenness is shown not only in the drinking of wine but in all things by which, both in contracts and in the business of the world, in losses and gains, in love and hatred, the mind is made drunk and wavers and cannot keep its state; and because we are encompassed by frail flesh and are compelled — for food and clothing and the necessities which pertain to the body — to do some things which we ought not to do, at least this is required of us: that — when we return into ourselves and know why we were born and enter the inner parts and shrines of the temple — we withdraw from the vices of the world and commit not even the least sins; by which it is shown both that we sin — when it is for the necessities of the flesh — light sins, and again that there is a time when — entering the inner court — we ought to be clean and estranged from all drunkenness.

44:22-31

A widow and a divorced woman (or a woman cast out) they shall not take as wives, but a virgin of the seed of the house of Israel; but also a widow who has been the widow of a priest they may take. And they shall teach my people; what the difference is between holy and polluted, between clean and unclean, they shall show them. And when there is a controversy (as is added in the Seventy, of blood), they shall stand in my judgments, and they shall judge; my laws and my precepts they shall keep in all my solemn feasts, and they shall sanctify my sabbaths. And they shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be polluted, except to father and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister who has not had another man: in these they shall be defiled. And after he has been cleansed, seven days shall be counted to him, and on the day of his entry into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister to me in the sanctuary, he shall offer for his sin, says the Lord God. But they shall have no inheritance; I am their inheritance, and you shall give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession. The victim both for sin and for trespass they shall eat, and every vow of Israel shall be theirs; and the first portions of all the firstborn, and all the libations of all that are offered, shall be the priests'; and the first portions of your foods you shall give to the priest, that he may lay up a blessing for his house. Anything that has died of itself or been caught by a beast, of birds or of cattle, the priests shall not eat. This whole passage contains precepts for the priests, who, after the many things which we have expounded above, are ordered not to take as wives a widow and a divorced woman, or one cast out — the widow and the divorced woman is the Synagogue, that is, the congregation of the Jews, which did not receive the Lord; hence the Synagogue is also rightly called 'cast out' or 'widow': but the one cast out is the throng of heretics, who went out from us because they were not of us —, but: A virgin, he says, of the seed of the house of Israel, who has been nurtured in the house of God, in the law and the prophets, of whom the Apostle also speaks: I wish to present you all as a holy virgin to Christ; this is the virgin of whom the divine word also says elsewhere: Love her and she will keep you, encircle her and she will exalt you, honor her that she may embrace you; and who the virgin is who is to be loved and guards her lover, he will know who has read this: Her I loved and sought from my youth, and I sought to take her as my bride, and I became a lover of her beauty; and the Lord of all loved her. And not only a virgin, but also a widow the priest ought to marry, one, however, who has been the wife of another priest: knowledge, namely, which another worshiper of God has found; for we ought not to be content with new teaching only, but also to cultivate the old and join it to our company, provided it has been trained in sacred worship. It is the office of the priest too to teach the people: What the difference is between holy and polluted, between clean and unclean, so that we refer the first to doctrines, the second to the works which are performed through the flesh — for who understands transgressions? —. And when there is a controversy 'about any matter' or, as the Seventy translated, 'of blood', that is, what pertains to a mortal crime: The priests shall stand in my judgments, so that they do not judge according to rank nor accept the person of poor or rich in judgment, but stand in the judgments of God — and remember that psalm: God has stood in the synagogue of gods, and in the midst he judges gods, calling 'gods' those who have the power of judging men —: for with what judgment they have judged, they themselves will be judged. My laws, he says, and my precepts they shall keep in all my solemn feasts, so that they may know how Christ our Passover was sacrificed, how we ought to fulfill seven weeks of joy and gladness, and humble our souls in fasting and in the sound of trumpets, and understand also spiritual feasts of Tabernacles — in which we say: I am a sojourner and a stranger, as all my fathers were —; these are the true solemn feasts of God, which one discussing the Pentateuch will interpret more fittingly: the first virtue of a priest is not only to teach what he knows, but to keep all the festivals of God, so that he may be able to command others to keep what he himself has observed — that it is the office of priests to have knowledge of the law we learn also in Malachi, who says: The lips of the priest shall guard knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts —. And they shall sanctify my sabbaths. And they shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be polluted (for which the Seventy translated: And they shall not go in upon the soul of a man, lest they be polluted), except to father, he says, and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister who has not had a man: they shall be defiled. And after he has been cleansed, seven days shall be counted to him, and on the day of his entry into the sanctuary and into the inner court, to minister to me in the sanctuary, he shall offer for his sin to the Lord God (or he shall offer a propitiation). And there shall be to them their inheritance, and you shall give them no possession in Israel, I am their possession, the priests are still being commanded; in which it must be observed that he did not say absolutely: and they shall sanctify 'sabbaths' — or, according to Isaiah: Your new moons and sabbaths my soul hates —, but with a distinction: 'my' sabbaths — hence it is written in the Gospel too: The priests in the temple violate the sabbath and are without blame: not the sabbath of God, but the sabbath of the letter, the sabbath of the Jews, which they rightly violate who are: A chosen race, a royal priesthood —; but the sabbath that has been sanctified let us understand as that which the Apostle too teaches has been left for the people of God — of which it is written: If they shall enter into my 'rest', which in Hebrew is called 'sabbath' —; and he sanctifies the sabbath of God who does not carry the burden of sin on the sabbath nor say: Like a heavy burden they have weighed heavy upon me: he who is such does not gather wood on the sabbath, nor build upon the foundation of Jesus Christ wood, hay, stubble, nor kindle a fire to consume useless material, and on the sabbath day he remains in one place and does not go outside, but remains set like a pillar in the temple of God — of which John writes in the Revelation: He who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go out no more —. As for what follows: And they shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be polluted: it belongs properly to the priestly office not to touch dead things, so that he who prays for the vices of others may himself approach the altar clean — of which dead the Savior too speaks in the Gospel: Leave the dead to bury their own dead —; these are defiled in a dead father when they forsake their Creator, and in a dead mother, departing from the Church, in a son also and a daughter, in that the one pertains to thoughts, the other to works — which is said more expressively in Greek, νοητὰ καὶ αἰσθητὰ [things of the mind and things of the senses] —; in brother also and sister: he who, reborn of the same spirit, if he has reckoned him dead, is defiled in him, only on this condition, if the sister has remained a virgin and not been stained by the embrace of any man — from which we understand the virginal privilege, that the contact of any man whatever takes away perfect purity; whether these things have been said rightly or wrongly, let us leave to the judgment of the reader —; the affection of nature too is approved herein, so that in the order of charity — according to what is written: Set charity in order in me —, after God the parent of all things, the father of the flesh too is loved, and the mother, son and daughter, brother and sister, only on this condition, if she has not gone out of the house nor passed into the power of another. And after the priest has been cleansed by the order of purification which is written in the Mosaic law: Seven days shall be counted to him — either the perfect number of penitence, or after the consummation of the world, when we have passed over to the true ogdoad —, that he may enter the Holy of Holies — for this is the inner court — and be able to minister in the sanctuary and always to offer a victim for the sin of conscience; and let there be no time in which he does not remember that he was stained over father and mother, son and daughter, brother and sister: for we are compelled to do many things, set as we are in the straits of this world, either by the condition of the flesh or by the frailty of nature. But he who shows himself such as to minister in the sanctuary and enter the inner court and always offer sacrifice to the Lord — so that, a true priest, he may be true, or rather an imitator of him of whom it is written: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek —, he shall have no inheritance except God, who is his inheritance, nor shall he receive a possession in Israel — that is, among the common crowd —, but a priestly one, so that the Lord may say of him: I am the inheritance and: I am their possession — whom, when they have found him, they will speak and say: I will hold him and will not let him go, and they will sing with the prophet: The Lord is my portion —. The victim both for sin and for trespass (or for ignorance) they shall eat, and every vow (or separation) in Israel shall be theirs; and the first portions of all the firstborn, and all the libations of all that are offered, shall be the priests'; and the first portions of your foods you shall give to the priest, that he may lay up a blessing for his house (or that he may put blessings upon your houses). For 'victim' and sacrifice, which in Hebrew is called 'manaa', Aquila and Symmachus translated 'gift'; again, for 'vow', which the Seventy translated ἀφόρισμα, that is, 'separation', Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion translated ἀνάθημα [a thing devoted], which in Hebrew is called 'herem'; and it must be considered that all the things which the Lord now speaks through the prophet he had already said before through Moses; and it must be asked why he repeats the same things that have been said: namely, that the things which are in the minds of men, blotted out either by negligence in reading or by contempt and forgetfulness in hearing, may be renewed by the living voice: things which are not written with pen and ink but by the Spirit and the Word of God — hence the Savior too left no volume of his teaching of his own, as the ravings of the apocrypha invent in many places, but by the Spirit of the Father and his own he speaks daily in the heart of believers —; and this will be the answer against those who slander the prophets: why they repeat in their own volumes what is contained in the Pentateuch. The victim, then, both for sin and for trespass (or ignorance) the priests are to eat — of whom it is written: They shall eat the sins of my people —; and we should not so much rejoice at the offering of gifts as fear the condemnation of our honor if we abuse it unworthily. The first portions, according to the letter, are those of living and lifeless things which are born first and which the earth first brings forth; the firstfruits of our foods too are offered to the priests, so that we taste nothing of the new crops unless the priest has tasted it first; and we do this so that the priest may lay up our blessing and offering in his house, or so that at his prayer the Lord may bless our houses: great is the dignity of priests, but great the ruin if they sin; we rejoice at the ascent, but let us fear the fall: it is not so great a joy to have held the heights as it is a grief to have fallen from the loftier places — for we shall render account not only for our own transgressions but for those of all whose gifts we abuse; and we are by no means anxious for their salvation —. Anything that has died of itself or been caught by a beast, of birds or of cattle, the priests shall not eat; and according to the letter these precepts befit every chosen race, royal and priestly — which refers properly to Christians, who have been anointed with the spiritual oil of which it is written: God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows —: that he not eat 'what has died of itself', whether of birds or of cattle, whose blood has not been shed — which in the Acts of the Apostles is called 'strangled', and that these things must necessarily be observed the letter of the apostles from Jerusalem warns — and what has been caught by a beast, because that too is likewise strangled: and it condemns priests who, out of the greed of the gullet, do not keep these things in the case of thrushes, figpeckers, dormice and other things of this kind. But according to ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense] we can call that dead of itself in which the blood of the soul has died, and which imitates 'Nabal' the Carmelite, whose name means 'fool', and who, when he heard of the wrath of David, trembled with fear: And his heart died within him; and caught by beasts — the beasts by whose bites the prophet sighs not to be torn, saying: Do not deliver to the beasts the soul that confesses you — must be said of him who is devoured by the bites of the adversary lion, and of the leopard which does not change its spots, and of the she-bear raging for her stolen cubs, and by the fury of wolves, and of the other beasts, which we take as the variety of demons; and the birds we say are those who set their mouth in heaven; and those cattle, the ones that, bent down and turned toward the earth, serve only the belly and the things that are below the belly.

45:1-8

And when you begin to divide the land as a possession, set apart firstfruits to the Lord, a sanctified portion of the land, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth; it shall be sanctified in all its border round about. And of this there shall be a sanctified portion five hundred by five hundred, four-square round about, and fifty cubits for its suburbs all around. And from this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand, and in it shall be the temple (or the sanctification) and the Holy of Holies. The sanctified portion of the land shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who approach to the ministry of the Lord; and it shall be a place for them for houses and for a sanctuary of holiness: twenty-five thousand of length and ten thousand of breadth. But the Levites who minister to the house, they shall possess twenty chambers (for which the Seventy translated: they shall hold a city to dwell in). And you shall give the possession of the city five thousand in breadth and twenty-five thousand in length, according to the separation of the sanctuary, to the whole house of Israel. To the prince also, on this side and on that, by the separation (or the firstfruits) of the sanctuary in the possession of the city, over against the face of the separation of the sanctuary and over against the face of the possession of the city, from the side of the sea to the sea and from the side of the east to the east, and of length along each part, from the western border to the eastern border, of the land: it shall be his possession in Israel, and the princes shall no more ravage (or lay waste) my people; and they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes. After the ceremonies of the priests, and their worship and their food — what they ought to take and what to avoid —, he now gives a description of the holy land; and before he divides the whole land among the tribes, he commands that out of all the tribes a place be chosen which should have twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth — and since 'of cubits' or 'of feet' or 'of ells' is not set down, we are given to understand that it signifies 'the reed', which was in the man's hand and had a measure of six cubits and a sixth part of one cubit, that is, a παλαιστήν [palm, a handbreadth]: let the diligent reader reckon how many reeds make a thousand paces and how many thousands there were in length and breadth —; after this description he again commanded that, from the sanctified land which was chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, that is, of twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth, another land within, of five hundred reeds round about, that is, of two thousand, be chosen for building the sanctuary, that is, the temple of the Lord. And lest perhaps other buildings should be joined to the building of the temple, he commanded that for fifty cubits round about the land be empty 'for suburbs', or, as Symmachus, Theodotion and the Seventy translated, 'for a boundary' and 'a separation' and 'a space'. When this description is finished, another measure, of a sanctification to be set apart, is prescribed afresh: that after the former measure another land be measured, of twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth, in which there is by no means the temple, that is, the holy place, but the Holy of Holies. And in it let the priests dwell who approach to the ministry of the Lord; and let them dwell there at the time when they discharge the priestly office: and let this possession be, as we have said, of twenty-five thousand reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth. Further, the Levites, who serve the priests and have ministries of their own, will receive a place for building twenty 'chambers' — according to Aquila; 'exedras' according to Symmachus; 'cells' according to Theodotion; or, as the Seventy translated, 'a city', by which we understand that a certain separate place for the dwelling of the Levites is called by the name of a city —, a place which is to have five thousand reeds in breadth and twenty-five thousand in length. All these things, that is, the sanctuary and the second sanctuary, and the Holy of Holies, and the dwellings of the priests and the houses of the Levites who minister to the priests, are called places separated and consecrated for ministry and for sanctification for the house of Israel. After the fourfold description of the holy land a fifth division is set down: that the prince or leader of the people should receive on this side and on that, that is, on either side of the sanctuary, for his possession, and should dwell in the city, and that his possession should face the place set apart for the temple and the face of the city, and should be from the side of the sea, that is, from the west, as far as the other side of the sea, having the breadth which the prophet describes below in the description of the individual tribes. Then follows: But in length along each part — which the individual tribes receive — from the western border — that is, of the sea — as far as the eastern border — where this ends we learn in the description of the tribes —; and this will be the possession of the leader or prince in the land of Israel. These things have been said for the present so that the plain account of the history may be known. But if we wish to compare spiritual things with spiritual and, following certain interpreters, to climb to higher things — they assert that the present things are a figure of things to come, and that all that is said pertains to the heavenly Jerusalem, which is the mother of us all, and to the Church of the firstborn —, it will not indeed be difficult to say what has been said by others, but we fear that the prudent reader may by no means accept an exposition of this kind; hence all things are to be referred both to the present time and to the Church, which now labors in the world and hastens to go to heavenly things: so that out of the whole world some are chosen as a possession of God to possess the holy place, and others, who have advanced to greater things, to hold the Holy of Holies; in the ministries too the order of priests and Levites is different: some of them daily offer sacrifice to God by their prayers and virtues, others are in a second and lesser rank, so as to minister to these, and through those who have climbed to the summits of the virtues; and last of all there is a leader or prince who has such power that he receives a possession over against one tribe and by the merit of one balances the merits of very many, and first, while he lives in the world, possesses the breadth from sea to sea, then from the west, or from the sea, as far as the east, so that, leaving the present things behind, he may hasten to the things to come, and may have his own fixed possession, and the prince may by no means desire what belongs to others, and each tribe may hold its own part: which can properly be referred to bishops and presbyters, to whom it is said that they should no more lay waste and ravage the people of God, nor possess the land of Israel as an inheritance, but that each should have his own possession, the one appointed to his rank. Now the twenty-five thousand they refer to the senses, which are set down four times; and the ten thousand to perfect knowledge, so that in the one only the plain history is held, while in the other there is discussion also of θεολογίᾳ [theology] and of the heavenly powers, because ten is a perfect number. This too must be considered: that the priests, who are set in the higher rank, possess twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth; but the rank of the Levites, that is, the lower one, has indeed the same number in length, that is, twenty-five thousand, but its breadth is bounded by the number five: hence too they hold only twenty chambers — the number in which the gifts for Esau are offered —; but the prince, who is truly a prince among the people and deserves to receive the name of leader, receives a possession of the sanctuary on this side and on that, namely from all who are subject to him of their own will, and he is a dweller in the city, and makes the salvation of many his own reward. In the first temple, which is called the sanctuary, five hundred reeds are described on each side, and again fifty cubits by which the whole possession of the priests is separated; but in the second sanctuary, where the Holy of Holies is, the breadth of the temple and its space are not described, but the number is uncertain: and this we find also in the possession of the prince, who has a possession among the people of Israel without any number, since the progress of all overflows to the prince: and the salvation of the disciples is the reward of the teachers.

45:9

Thus says the Lord God: Let it suffice you, princes in Israel; leave off iniquity and plunder, and do judgment and righteousness: separate your borders from my people, says the Lord God. For 'plunder' the Seventy translated 'misery'; for 'borders', 'oppression'. And the sense is: 'Since you have received your portion, O princes — as Scripture says: To the prince also on this side and on that, in the separation of the sanctuary, in the possession of the city (understand: you shall give) —, and your power is so great that your possession has received the portion of one tribe: therefore I command and admonish you that it suffice to have committed iniquity and plunder up to now, while you invade and snatch away what belongs to others; and — since it is written: Put away evil and do good, and conversely: Do judgment and righteousness, judging for the orphan and justifying the widow —: Separate your borders from my people, namely so that you do not move the boundaries, and because the very neighborhood harms the humbler man, who cannot bear the haughtiness of one greater and more powerful. Let this be said for the present to the people of that time; but the command can also be fitted to our own princes — who after the manner of Pharaoh and the Egyptians oppress the children of Israel through their power, and do not remember that it is written: Have they made you leader? Do not be lifted up, but be among them as one of them —, and also that which the Lord says in the Gospel κατὰ [according to] Luke: But if that servant says in his heart: My master delays to come; and begins to beat his men-servants and maid-servants, and to eat and drink and be drunk: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect and at an hour that he does not know, and will divide him, and will put his portion with the unbelievers; his disciples too he instructs with these precepts in the Gospel according to Matthew: You know that the princes of the nations lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise power over them; it shall not be so among you, but whoever wishes to be great among you shall become your minister, and whoever wishes to be first, let him be the servant of all. Just as the Son of man came not to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give his life as a redemption for many: there are many passages, if I wished to unroll them from the sacred Scriptures, where the pride of the greater is restrained and all are called to the humility of the Lord, who says: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart.

Book Fourteen

What I ought to have said at the beginning of Ezekiel's temple I am now about to say at the end, in reversed order, mindful of that little verse: Here is that toil of the house and the inextricable wandering, of which the same poet also sings in another place: As once in lofty Crete the Labyrinth is said to have held a path woven between blind walls, and a treacherous deceit of a thousand ways, where the undetectable and irretraceable wandering would break the tokens for following. So I too, having entered the ocean of the holy Scriptures and, so to speak, the labyrinth of the mysteries of God — of which it is written: He made darkness his hiding place and: Clouds round about him —, do not dare to claim for myself a perfect knowledge of the truth, but only to have offered to those who desire to know some indications of the teaching: not by my own strength but by the mercy of Christ, who, while we were wandering, ... himself unravels the deceits and windings of the house, guiding the blind by the Holy Spirit footsteps. Following him, we shall be able to reach the harbor of the explanations of the prophet Ezekiel, toward which this book is the last, that is, the fourteenth; and if, with you praying, virgin of Christ Eustochium, I bring it through to the end, and the Lord grants the span of this life, I shall pass over to Jeremiah, who alone of the prophets remains for us; and his interpretation will be indeed of my labor and of your prayers, but properly of the clemency of Christ.

45:10-12

A just balance and a just 'oephi' and a just batus you shall have; the 'oephi' and the batus shall be equal and of one measure, so that the batus holds a tenth part, and the 'oephi' a tenth part: according to the measure of the 'corus' shall be their equal balancing. And the shekel has twenty obols; moreover, twenty shekels and twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels make a mina. (LXX: "A just balance and a just measure and a just choenix you shall have for measure, and likewise there shall be one choenix for receiving: the tenth part of the gomer the choenix, and the tenth part of the gomer the 'oephi'; in relation to the gomer it shall be equal, and for weight twenty obols: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.") This passage, according to the Seventy, does not hang together and cannot be understood at all, since they changed not only the numbers of the measures but also the names: for in place of 'oephi' they translated 'measure', a general name for a specific one, and in place of 'batus' 'choenix'; in place of the Hebrew 'omer' too, which in Greek is called 'corus', they translated 'gomor', and again in place of 'batus' 'choenix'. Let us therefore speak according to the Hebrew and the letter, and let us explain more plainly what seems right to us in each particular. The 'balance', which in Hebrew is called 'mozene', is understood of the things that are weighed; but the 'epha', which in the Greek language is corruptly called 'oephi', pertains to the measure of various crops, for example wheat, barley, legumes; moreover the 'batus', which in Hebrew is called 'bath', is the same measure as the 'oephi', and only in liquid kinds, wine and oil and other things of this sort; the 'corus' holds thirty modii, and in both measures, that is, of dry things as well as of liquids, it holds the first place; the tenth part of the 'corus', in things that are measured by the modius, is called 'epha' — that is, three modii — and the tenth part of the 'corus' in liquid kinds is called 'batus' or 'badus': so that the 'epha' and the 'batus' are of the same measure; moreover the 'siclus' [shekel], which in Greek is called 'stater', has twenty obols; but the 'mina', which in Greek is called 'mna', has sixty shekels, which make one thousand two hundred obols; but what he says: Twenty shekels and twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels make a mina, ought not to disturb the reader: for the difficulty is placed in the numbers for this reason, to make the hearer's mind attentive — whence also many things are spoken in parables and riddles, as: He who has ears to hear, let him hear; and all prophecy contains the truth in obscurity, so that the disciples may hear within, while the ignoble crowd placed outside may not know what is being said —. The divine Scripture therefore commanded that weights be just — saying: There shall not be in your purse a large measure and a smaller. A true and just balance you shall have, and a true and just measure you shall have; and in Proverbs it is said: A large balance and a smaller, both are abominable in the sight of God —, which indeed is to be observed by us not only in commerce and in the use of daily life, but righteousness must be guarded in all things — as Scripture says: By your words you shall make a balance and a weight —, so that, in words and in deed and in thoughts, we may do all things by weight and reason. That the obol, that is, the twentieth part of the 'siclus' or stater, is the smallest little portion, we read in another place: To the one who is faithful, the whole world of riches; but to the one who is unfaithful, not even an obol — as if he had said in other words: 'The unfaithful man possesses nothing in the world, but lacks even the smallest portion', of which it is said in another word in the Gospel: He shall not come out from there until he pays the last quadrans, that is, even the very last and smallest coin —; we read of ten minas handed over to individual servants for trading, and in another parable of talents divided among servants, and of the debtor of five hundred denarii, and of fifty, and of the laborers of the vineyard who each receive a denarius, and of the widow woman who lost a drachma and scarcely found it again by lighting a lamp: what sense all these things have, this is not the time to discuss.

45:13-14

And these are the firstfruits which you shall take: the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of grain, and the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of barley. The measure of oil also, a batus of oil, is the tenth part of a 'corus'; and ten bati make a 'corus', because ten bati fill a 'corus'. (LXX: "And these are the firstfruits which you shall set apart: the sixth part of a measure from a gomor of wheat and the sixth part of an 'oephi' from a 'corus' of barley. And the ordinance of the oil: a cotyle — that is, a cyathus — of oil from ten cotylae, because ten cotylae are a gomor.") Here too, the names of the measures having been changed, everything in the edition of the Seventy is confused, so that what is said cannot be understood: for they who above had said 'measure' for 'oephi', and 'choenix' for 'batus', and 'gomor' for 'corus', 'weight' for 'siclus', here too say 'measure' for 'oephi', for 'corus' now 'gomer', now 'corus' itself, and in the measure of oil 'cotyle', that is, 'cyathus', for 'batus'. Let us therefore speak first according to the letter. Δεκάτας — that is, the tenth part — of all crops the people owed by the law to the Levitical tribe; again, from these very tithes the rank of the Levites — that is, of the lower ministers — gave tithes to the priests, and this is what is called δεύτερον δεκάτη [the second tithe] — there were also other tithes, which each one of the people of Israel set apart in his own granaries, so that he might eat them when he went to the temple in the city of Jerusalem, and in the vestibule of the temple they would invite both priests and Levites to banquets; and there were also other tithes, which they stored up for the poor, which in the Greek language are called πτωχοδεκάται [poor-tithes] —; but the firstfruits which they offered from their crops were not defined by a specific number but left to the discretion of those offering, and we have received a tradition of the Hebrews, not commanded by the law but grown into custom by the discretion of the teachers: he who gave the most gave the fortieth part to the priests, he who gave the least the sixtieth; between the fortieth and the sixtieth it was permitted to offer whatever they wished; what therefore was left doubtful in the Pentateuch is here specifically defined on account of the avarice of the priests, so that they may not exact more from the people in the bringing of firstfruits, that is: that they offer the sixtieth part of the things that grow from the earth — for if the 'corus', which in Hebrew is called 'omer' and by the Seventy is called 'gomer', holds thirty modii in dry kinds as well as in liquids, and the 'epha' and the 'batus' too, according to what we said above, are the tenth part of the 'corus', and it is commanded that the sixth part both of the 'oephi' and of the 'batus' be given to the priests in offering the firstfruits, which out of three modii makes half a modius, it is clearly reckoned that the priests ought to receive the sixtieth part as firstfruits —. Let it suffice for the meantime to have perceived and heard these things according to the letter and according to the Hebrew truth. Now let us return to the spiritual understanding, in which it must first be asked how it is said: 'Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and give him the firstfruits of the fruits of your righteousness, so that your storerooms may be filled with grain, and your winepresses may overflow with wine, so that, after you have offered the firstfruits of your labors and virtues and have said: Behold, now I have brought you the firstfruits of the fruits of the earth, which you gave me, O Lord, you may deserve to hear: Blessed are you in the city and blessed in the field; blessed the children of your womb and the produce of your land, and the fruit of your beasts and so on, and you may possess — according to the Apostle — every blessing of spiritual things in the heavenly places in Christ, while you hold that whatever you have is not of your own virtue but of the mercy of him who gave the crops'. And if indeed we have so much knowledge of the Scriptures that we lay open all the mystical things and teach men, that is, the rational animal, we give the firstfruits of our grain; but if, after ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], we follow only the pure history, which can nourish the simple — according to what is written: Men and beasts you will save, O Lord —, we give the firstfruits of our barley — which barley: Isaac also served in the land of the foreigners, and it rose for him a hundredfold —. He who gives the firstfruits of barley can say: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing: in a place of pasture, there he has placed me, beside the waters of refreshment he has brought me up, but he who feeds rational living creatures with grain turns the sentence and says: You have prepared a table in my sight against those who trouble me, and after he has offered the firstfruits of oil and wine he joins on and says: You have anointed my head with oil, and your cup that inebriates, how splendid it is: with that oil which is prepared, most pure, without dregs, for the lamp of the Lord — and whoever has prepared it: His face is gladdened with oil, with the oil of exultation with which Christ was anointed above his fellows, and, made an olive tree, he will sing with the prophet: But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God —, and with that wine which overflows from the true vine in the winepresses of the Savior — as the Lord says: I am the vine, you the branches, my Father the vinedresser —; of these winepresses we read three psalms, Psalm 8, Psalm 80 (81) and Psalm 83 (84), all of which refer to the mysteries of the Church. And indeed in the old law the firstfruits were without measure and number: For God did not give the Spirit by measure; but in the second building of the temple, which the prophecy of Ezekiel contains, there is a fixed measure, that is, the number sixty: by which the world is filled up, and it is said to us: With whatever measure you have measured, it will be measured back to you.

45:15-17

And one ram from a flock of two hundred, from those which they nourish in Israel, for a sacrifice and for a holocaust and for peace offerings, to make expiation for them, says the Lord God. All the people of the land shall be bound to these firstfruits for the prince of Israel; and upon the prince shall be the holocausts and the sacrifice and the libations, at the solemnities and at the calends and at the sabbaths: at all the solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall make the sacrifice for sin and the holocaust and the peace offerings, to make expiation for the house of Israel. Above he said what portion of the things that are weighed, and of the measures too, both of dry kinds and of liquids, ought to be offered to the prince; now he keeps the same order of firstfruits in living creatures, and commands Israel to offer one out of a flock of two hundred rams: Which Israel nourishes, for a sacrifice and for a holocaust and for peace offerings, to make expiation for the people of Israel, says the Lord God. What we translated: From those which Israel nourishes, is written in the Hebrew 'memmasce', which Aquila and Symmachus translate ἀπὸ τῶν ὑδάτων, the Seventy and Theodotion ἀπὸ τῶν ποτιστηρίων: of which the one means from irrigated places, the other from channels or pools, so that, evidently, the firstfruits of the prince are nourished nowhere else but in irrigated places. And as in the preceding we read that the sixtieth part of the things that are weighed and that are subject to measure ought to be offered to the prince, so now the two-hundredth part of the living creatures is commanded to be offered, and the whole people is subject to the precept of this law and of this command: that it offer to the leader or prince, because, of course, through him holocausts and sacrifices and libations are offered for the people at each solemnity, and the house of God is expiated; from which it is to be noticed that, as the people is debtor to offer firstfruits to the prince, so the prince is debtor to the people to offer victims for it; and him, according to tropology, we can understand as none other than God the Savior. He receives a ram out of two hundred living creatures — or, as the Hebrew word shows more significantly, βόσκημα [a grazing beast], which can refer to all living creatures and not properly to a ram —, and he receives the animal or ram which has been nourished in irrigated places, namely those of the holy Scriptures, and can say: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing: into a place of pasture, there he has placed me, beside the waters of refreshment he has brought me up; these were the irrigated places, nay rather these the channels, to which Jacob too led his flocks, so that in them they might drink and conceive and, according to the color of the rods, bring forth offspring for the Lord. In place of 'sacrifice', that is, θυσίᾳ, Aquila and Symmachus translate 'gift', which in the Hebrew is called 'manaa', and it properly pertains not to a victim but to the things which are offered in sacrifice from fine flour and parched grain and oil; but the 'holocaust' is what is offered whole to God and consumed by the sacred fire; the 'peace offerings', when we are reconciled to God: and on our behalf the Apostle says: We pray on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God, and in another place: God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself. But this prince, to whom the firstfruits of living creatures are offered, is himself the king, as is shown also in the title of the cross in Hebrew and Greek and Latin letters — and when the Jews strove to have the triumphal title taken down, the throng of the Gentiles, in Pilate, answered: What I have written, I have written —. Upon the prince, he says, shall be: finely is the priestly dignity reminded to what office it is subject, so that it may know that it ought to offer for the people the sacrifice and the libations which are offered from wine at all the solemnities: namely at the calends, that is, the new moons, as well as at the sabbaths, when, with darkness covering all things, there is the beginning of the moon's light, in the rest of the sabbaths: so that he may make, namely, for sin, to make expiation for the house of Israel, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and bulwark of the truth: for this is the house of the living God and the house of Israel, which needs the expiation of its sins.

45:18-25

Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you shall take a calf from the herd without blemish, and you shall expiate the sanctuary. And the priest shall take of the blood of what will be for sin, and shall put it on the doorposts of the house and on the four corners of the ledge of the altar and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court. And thus you shall do on the seventh of the month for each one who was ignorant and was deceived by error, and you shall make expiation for the house. In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a solemnity; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten. And the prince shall make on that day, for himself and for all the people of the land, a calf for sin; and in the solemnity of seven days he shall make as a holocaust to the Lord seven calves and seven rams without blemish daily for seven days, and for sin a he-goat of the goats daily; and the sacrifice he shall make of an 'oephi' for each calf and an 'oephi' for each ram, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi'. In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the solemnity he shall do as has been said above, for seven days, both for sin and for the holocaust, and in sacrifice and in oil. (I have set down the whole chapter so that, divided into its single parts, it should not confuse the reader's mind; and first we must speak about the variety of the translation; where we translated: On the four corners of the ledge of the altar, the Seventy translated: And upon the four corners of the temple and upon the altar; and where we said: For each one who was ignorant and was deceived by error, they put: For the ignorant and the little one; also in the place where we said: And the sacrifice he shall make of an 'oephi' for each calf, an 'oephi', and an 'oephi' for each ram, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi', their edition has: And the sacrifice and a cooking for the calf and a cooking for the ram you shall give, and a 'hin' of oil for the cooking; in the last little verse too, where we said: In sacrifice and in oil, they said: As in the manaa, as in the oil.) In the first, he says, month and on the first day of the month — no doubt he means Nisan —, and: You shall take a calf from the herd, not one which has been nourished at home but one in the herd, that is, from the flock and number of many; on the seventh day of the same month too: these two solemnities, that is, the first day of the first month and the seventh of the same, are not found in the Mosaic law; but the fourteenth day of the month, on which the Passover is celebrated, Moses too commanded to be observed: when we eat unleavened bread for seven days; but the fourth solemnity, of which he says: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the solemnity and so on, seems to me to signify the Scenopegia [the feast of Tabernacles], which he has set down here without a name. Let us run back, then, to the particulars, and briefly discuss what seems right to us. That there are spiritual solemnities too the Apostle teaches: Let no one therefore judge you in food or in drink or in solemnities or of the new moon or of sabbaths, which are a shadow of things to come; and if God says through Isaiah: Your new moons and your sabbaths and the great day I do not accept: the fast and the holidays and your new moons and solemnities my soul hates, it is manifest that he who hates the solemnities of the Jews loves his own, namely the sabbath which is left for the people of God: That we may see the things that have been given to us by God: and may speak not in the learned words of human wisdom, but in the teaching of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual: for in the present age, which is set in the evil one, we cannot see good days, but in the new, of which days the Holy Spirit sings in the Mosaic song: Remember the days of antiquity, understand the years of the generation of generations, of which the holy man also spoke in the psalm: In the night I meditated in my heart, and again: And I had the eternal years in mind and I meditated; let him who has not accepted this understanding answer how he can expound what Isaiah prophesies about the future and new age: There shall be month from month and sabbath from sabbath, and all flesh shall come to worship the Lord, when the true worshipers will by no means worship on Mount Gerizim nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth, when there will be a new heaven and a new earth and: The whole creation shall be freed from the servitude of corruption into the liberty of the children of God and the sun will receive seven times as much light and the moon will be compared to the sun: We have come, indeed, to Mount 'Sion', which means 'watchtower', and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to thousands of angels' solemnities, of which solemnity another prophet also speaks: What will you do in the days of assembly and in the days of the solemnity of the Lord? this is what is also said elsewhere: Celebrate, Judah, your festivals, pay your vows. If then we have learned spiritual solemnities, we shall consequently be taught spiritual victims too: a calf is taken from the herd — or a bull, as Symmachus translated —, free and pressed by no yoke, that is, by the burden of sins, and without blemish: Who did no sin, nor was guile found in his mouth, a young calf putting forth horns and hoofs: so that in him the sanctuary may be cleansed and expiated. And the priest, he says, shall take of its blood which will be for the sin of all, who in other words is called a lamb in Exodus, and in the Gospel, as John the Baptist says: Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world; and the blood itself is precious, in which we are redeemed in the passion of the Lord Savior, by whose flesh we are fed and with whose blood we are given drink, by which are touched the four corners of the ledge of the 'altar' — for which Theodotion put the Hebrew word itself, 'azara' [ledge, court], or of the 'temple', as the Seventy translated —, so that the house and the altar may be sanctified — for all the elements of the world are sanctified by this blood — so that, when someone has been expiated and cleansed, he may enter the gate of the inner court and be able to know the secrets of the Lord, and consequently come to the seventh day of the first month and attain rest and offer sacrifice to the Lord: both for ignorance — of which David speaks: The sins of my youth and of my ignorance remember not —, and for the little one — who, when he has come to the measure of the perfect man, destroys the things that belong to a little one and speaks confidently: When I was a little one, I spoke as a little one, I thought as a little one —, or for him who was deceived by error and sinned not so much by will as by the supposition of good. And when the two solemnities of the first month have been completed, that is, of the first day and of its seventh, he comes to the fourteenth day of the month, on which is the solemnity of the Passover, of which it is written: For our Passover has been sacrificed, Christ; then we eat unleavened bread for seven days in rest and security of all things, when, destroying the leaven of malice and wickedness, we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, while our prince offers all these things for us: and first 'for himself' — for he took up a human body and for sin destroyed sin, he who grieves for us and bears our infirmities —, then 'for his house' — which is written in the Seventy but is not found in the Hebrew — that is, for the Church, and for all the people of the land, namely the whole human race: He is the Savior, indeed, of all men and especially of the faithful; and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not only for us, but for the whole world. And when the calf has been offered for all the people of the land, on the seven remaining days of the Lord's passion seven calves and seven rams without blemish are offered daily, so that they may be burned up as a holocaust and by the Lord's fire: and the seven calves and seven rams are those who are conformed to the Lord's passion, so that they may imitate the true calf and the true ram, and by the blood of the martyrs through seven days the sins of the whole world may be cleansed; a he-goat of the goats too is offered for sin daily, namely for seven days. And it must be noted more carefully that in the sacrifice an 'oephi' for each calf and an 'oephi' for each ram and a 'hin' of oil are offered, which are commanded by the law, but in the offering of the he-goat neither an 'oephi' nor, as the Seventy translated, a 'cooking' is set down — they who for 'oephi' translated πέμμα, that is, 'cooking' —; but the 'hin', which is a fixed measure of oil, of which we have already spoken before, is taken up in the sacrifice of the calf and of the ram, so that we may receive the fuel of everlasting light, and rest from labor, and healing from weariness after the appeasement of sins. In the seventh month too, on the fifteenth day of the month, that is, of the Scenopegia, the same order of oblation and sacrifices is to be kept: Both for sin and for the holocaust and in sacrifice and in oil, so that, darkness having been put to flight and the light of the oil having risen, we may attain the festival of the Lord, and may have brighter solemnities, in which all our sins are forgiven us.

46:1-7

Thus says the Lord God: The gate of the inner court that faces toward the east shall be shut on the six days on which work is done; but on the sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the kalends also it shall be opened, and the prince shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate from outside, and shall stand on the threshold of the gate, and the priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings, and he shall worship upon the threshold of the gate, and shall go out; but the gate shall not be shut until evening. And the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate on the sabbaths and kalends before the Lord. And this holocaust the prince shall offer to the Lord on the sabbath day: six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish, and a sacrifice of an 'oephi' for the ram, but for the lambs a sacrifice such as his hand shall give, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi'; but on the day of the kalends: a calf from the herd without blemish, and six lambs and a ram shall be without blemish, and an 'oephi' for the calf, an 'oephi' also for the ram he shall make as a sacrifice, but for the lambs as his hand shall find, and a 'hin' of oil for each 'oephi'. Where we have translated 'oephi', which is the tenth part of a 'corus', the Seventy translated πέμμα, which in our language means 'cooking'; and where we said 'sacrifice', they set down the Hebrew word itself, 'manaa', which Aquila translated 'gift' or 'sacrifice', Theodotion 'sacrifice'. And meanwhile, before we discuss what these things signify, the very words of Scripture must be laid open παραφραστικῶς [by way of paraphrase]. The gate, he says, of the inner court on six days — of which it is written: Six days you shall labor and do all your works — shall be shut, and not just any gate, but the one that faces toward the east, whence the sun of righteousness rises; further, on the sabbath day, that is, the seventh, on which there is rest, it will be opened every week, and again, when thirty days are completed, when there is the end of one month and the beginning of another, on the new moon, namely the day of the kalends, it will be opened, so that the privilege the seventh day has in the week, the beginning of the month may have as its privilege too. But why the gate of the inner court that faces toward the east is opened on the seventh day and on the day of the kalends, the following discourse will show: And the prince shall enter, he says, by the way of the gate from outside — namely of the outer court —, and shall stand on the threshold of the gate — of the inner court, which faces the east —, and he shall not enter the inner court, but, while he stands, other priests are to make for him the 'holocaust' — which Symmachus translated 'offering' —, and the peace offerings — or those which pertain to salvation —, so that, after the prince's victim has been burned up by the sacred fire and the leader has been reconciled to God, he may then worship upon the threshold of the gate of the inner court on which he has stood, and go out. What then? After the prince's going out will the gate be shut at once? By no means, but it will be open until evening, so that after the prince: All the people of the land may worship before the entrance of that gate: and they are to worship on the sabbaths and on the kalends, when the gate is opened. And since he had said above: The priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings, and had not indicated the number of the holocaust, he now adds: And this holocaust the prince shall offer to the Lord on the sabbath day — he will offer it, however, not by himself, but through the priests, of whom it is written: And the priests shall make his holocaust and his peace offerings —: six, he says, lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish, so that the sacrifice of the ram is the measure of an 'oephi' — which in Hebrew is called 'epha' —, while for the six lambs the sacrifice is what the hand of the one who offers was able to offer, and for each 'oephi' there will be the measure of oil that is called 'hin'; but the kalends, that is, the day of the new moons, had this privilege beyond the sabbath day, that: A calf from the herd (or a bull) without blemish be sacrificed, while the rest, that is, the six lambs without blemish and the ram without blemish and their sacrifices, will keep the rite of the sabbath, only in such a way that, just as with the ram an 'oephi' of sacrifice is offered, that is, of fine flour, and a 'hin' of oil, so it is offered with the calf too. Let these things be set down for the sake of clarity; now, the Lord granting, let us unfold the spiritual sense.
